# Moonframe components

Everything a mod can draw. Prefer, in order: a component that fits, a
component with a `class` and a `style.luau` rule, a composition of
components, and only then new `ui.*` code. See the moonframe skill for
how mods, styles and providers work.

## Host elements

The `ui.*` functions the host draws itself. Components are built from these.
Text-like elements take their main value positionally: `ui.text "hi"`,
`ui.button { "Save", msg = "save" }`.

### Layout

| Element | Use it for | Keys (besides children) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui.row { ... }`, `ui.column { ... }` | any box of children; with `msg`/`command` the whole box is clickable (rows, tabs, tiles); `drag = true` makes it a title bar that moves the window | frame keys, `align`, `justify`, `wrap`, `selected`, `drag`, `key` (names it among its siblings: with a `transition` rule it grows in as it appears and shrinks away as it goes; with `rise` it fills its box and comes up from below it whole, once the one it replaces has sunk away), `msg`/`to`, `command` or `window` (a mod opened in a window of its own), pointer keys, extras |
| `ui.panel { ... }` | a titled section with header actions over a body | frame keys, `title`, `actions = { elements }` |
| `ui.hsplit { ... }`, `ui.vsplit { ... }` | areas the user resizes by dragging; children must be `ui.pane` | `id` |
| `ui.pane { ... }` | one side of a split; slides in and out when `visible` changes; `lazy = true` starts what it mounts only once it first shows, and keeps it asleep (not run, not drawn) while hidden | `size`, `min`, `max`, `fixed`, `visible`, `lazy`, `gap`, `padding`, `surface`, `scroll` |
| `ui.list { count = n, row_height = 24, row = function(i) ... end }` | long lists of same-height rows (files, logs, results): only the rows that show are built and drawn, so any length costs a screenful; it scrolls itself and takes the space it is given | `id` (two lists in one mod need two), `count`, `row_height`, `row` (builds row `i`, from 1; called again as it scrolls, so keep it cheap), frame keys |
| `ui.region "name"` | the slot mods fill by naming it in `region` (shell only) | `name`, `direction`, `gap`, `justify` |
| `ui.mount "name"` | one mod's view, by name | `mod` |
| `ui.divider()` | a line across the parent's axis | |
| `ui.spacer()` | take the free space, to push what follows to the far end | |

### Content

| Element | Use it for | Keys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui.text "..."` | any text; a bare string child is plain text | `text`, `tone`, `size`, `weight` (`light` `normal` `medium` `semibold` `bold`), `truncate` (one line), `lines` (at most N lines), `wrap = false` (keep lines whole, for code that scrolls sideways), `syntax` (color it as code in this language, a line at a time), extras |
| `ui.icon "name"` | a bundled icon at the text's size and color; `spin = true` turns it (loaders). Lucide glyphs (git: `git-branch` `git-commit-horizontal` `git-merge` `git-pull-request` `git-pull-request-draft` `git-pull-request-closed` `git-compare` `circle-dot`), agent logos `agent-claude` `agent-codex` `agent-gemini` `agent-cursor` `agent-copilot` `agent-opencode` `agent-amp` `agent-droid` `agent-kiro` `agent-qwen` `agent-grok`, brands `brand-github` `brand-gitlab` `brand-anthropic` `brand-openai` `brand-mistral` `brand-ollama`; the full list is `IconName` in types/moonframe.d.luau | `name`, `tone`, `size`, `spin`, extras |
| `ui.image "avatar.png"` | a picture from a file inside the app's folders or `~/.cache/moonframe/images` (relative to the mod, `~/`, or absolute; no URLs: a provider downloads into that cache); `radius` rounds it into an avatar | `src`, `width`, `height`, `fit` (`contain` `cover` `fill` `scale-down` `none`), `zoom` (screen pixels per picture pixel, 1 is 100 %: a viewer that fills its parent unless sized) panned to `center = { x, y }` (fractions of the picture), `overlay = { elements }` drawn over the picture wherever it lands (their `area` is in fractions of the picture: a crop frame, spots), `measure` (sent with the picture's `width`, `height`, `box_width`, `box_height` and the `fit` zoom when they change), extras |
| `ui.badge "..."` | a small pill: counts, tags, states | `text`, `tone`, extras |
| `ui.terminal { id = "main" }` | a live shell that fills its space | `id`, `cwd`, `engine` (`alacritty`, `ghostty`), `exit` (sent once, with `exited = true` added, as the shell exits; without it Enter starts another) |
| `ui.browser { id = "docs", url = "https://..." }` | a web page in a native view that fills its space (macOS, Windows; Linux offers the system browser); drive it with `command = "browser-back"` (`-forward`, `-reload`, `-stop`) and `browser = "<id>"` on a control | `id`, `url` (http, https, file), `zoom`, `navigate` (sent with `url`, `title`, `loading`, `back`, `forward` added) and `loading` (with `loading`, `url`); a `ui.input { browser = "<id>" }` is its address bar |
| `ui.markdown "# Notes"` | a markdown document drawn by the host (headings, emphasis, lists, task lists, tables, quotes, `> [!NOTE]` alerts, footnotes, frontmatter, highlighted code with a copy button; LaTeX in a build with `math`), up to 1 MiB; links send `link` instead of opening, a `#heading` link scrolls there, a `[label](cite:source)` link draws a source chip, and pictures show only with `images`, never from the web; styled by `markdown`, `markdown-code`, `markdown-quote`, `markdown-alert`, `markdown-find` and `markdown-find-current` rules | `text`, `link` (sent with `url` added), `to`, `grow`, `scroll`, `width`, `height`, `max_width`, `lines` (at most N lines, for a preview), `images`, `image` (a click on a picture on its own line, with `src` and `alt`), `outline` (sent with `headings`: `level`, `text`, `at`, `slug`), `section` (sent with `heading`, the index being read), `reveal = { at, seq }` (scrolls there when it changes), `find`, `find_index`, `found` (sent with `count`), `stream` (fade in what is added) |
| `ui.paths { paths = { { points = { 0, 8, 40, 8, 40, 30 }, arrow = "end", radius = 6 } } }` | lines the view places in pixels from its top-left corner: arrows between dependent bars, connectors in a diagram; without `width` and `height` it fills its parent, so it floats over what it links (`float = "fill"` on a wrapper) | `paths` (each `points` flat x, y pairs, `color`, `stroke`, `dashed`, `radius` rounds its corners, `arrow` `end` `start` `both`), `width`, `height` |
| `ui.map { pins = { { lat = 37.79, lon = -122.40, label = "1" } } }` | a street map from a tile provider with numbered pins and routes over it; drag pans, the wheel, a pinch, a two-finger double tap, a double click and its buttons zoom, and two fingers turn it (it settles on north within a few degrees); without `center`/`zoom` it frames the pins and routes. With `glide`, a new `center`, `zoom` or `bearing` eases the map there. Tiles come only from the listed providers, cached under the cache folder; the provider's credit shows in the corner. Built with the `map` feature (the starter and sealed apps using it have it; elsewhere it marks its spot) | `provider` (`openstreetmap`, the default, and `carto-light` `carto-dark` `carto-voyager` `esri-streets` need no key; `stadia-smooth` `stadia-smooth-dark` `maptiler-streets` `mapbox-streets` `thunderforest-transport` need `key`), `center = { lat, lon }`, `zoom`, `bearing` (the compass direction up the box, degrees clockwise from north; a new one turns the map where it stands, so feed `move`'s back in and a compass shown while it is not 0 sets it to 0 on a click), `pins` (each `lat`, `lon`, `label` up to 3 characters or `icon`, `color`, `shape` `dot` `disc` `balloon`, `selected`, `pulse` (a halo breathes out of it: where the user is), `msg`), `routes` (each `points` flat lat, lon pairs drawn as they are, or `via` stops and `mode` `walk` `bike` `car` routed along streets by routing.openstreetmap.de; `color`, `stroke`, `dashed`; the style's `color` otherwise), `routed` (sent with `route`, `seconds`, `meters` once a `via` route is found), `move` (sent with `lat`, `lon`, `zoom`, `bearing` after the user moves it, as they go), `select` (sent with `pin`, its index, on a click), `to`, `width`, `height`, `grow` |
| `ui.video { source = "camera", white = 4095 }` | live frames from another process, from a ring in shared memory, in a 16-bit colour-managed native view that fills its space (macOS, the `video` feature); nothing draws over it, so `guides` draws crop frames and lines in the picture. `source`, `id`, `zoom`, `center`, `filter` (`auto` `nearest` `linear`), `color` (`srgb` `display-p3` `rec709` `rec2020` `linear-srgb` `linear-p3` `none`), `extended`, `black`, `white`, `gain`, `gamma`, `guides`, `probe`, `stats`, `probed`, `width`, `height`. Most apps want `video-viewer`; see `docs/video.md` |
| `ui.view { name = "chart", id = "sales", props = {...} }` | a view the app writes in Rust and registers by `name` (apps on the Moonframe library; the starter registers none): what Luau can't draw, such as an editor or a canvas. Kept by mod and `id`, it gets `props` again when they change, and sends this mod's `update` messages of its own | `name`, `id`, `props`, `class`, `style` |

### Controls

| Element | Use it for | Keys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui.button { "Label", ... }` | an action with a label and/or an icon (`icon` alone is an icon-only button) | `label`, `icon`, `variant`, `small`, `disabled`, `msg`/`to` or `command`, extras |
| `ui.item { "Label", ... }` | a plain selectable list row | `label`, `detail`, `badge`, `selected`, `msg`/`to` or `command`, extras |
| `ui.input { id = "title", value = state.title, change = "type" }` | a text field the host edits (`multiline` for a text area); what the user typed stays across renders, `value` replaces it when the mod passes a new one. A writing field with `prose` (markdown styled as typed), `dim = "sentence"` or `"paragraph"` (focus mode: the rest fades) and `typewriter` (the caret's line stays in the middle), as `prose-editor` draws it | `id`, `value`, `placeholder`, `change` (each edit, with `value` and `caret`, the bytes before the caret), `select` (selection movement, also with `value`, `caret` and `selected`, the bytes selected), `submit` (Enter, or ⌘↩ when multiline), `blur` (with `value`, as it loses focus: save a title edited in place), `keys`, `capture` (every chord pressed, with `keys` added, instead of editing: records a shortcut), `to`, `multiline`, `rows`, `max_rows` (grows with its lines up to it), `focus`, `disabled`, `mono`, `width`, `grow`, `browser`, `prose`, `dim`, `typewriter` |

### Overlays

| Element | Use it for | Keys |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ui.popover { ..., content = el }` | content floating beside its anchor (the children): dropdowns, context menus, sheets from a status bar; `side` is `top`, `bottom`, `left` or `right` (it opens on the other side when that one has no room in the window), and `align` (`start`, `end`) the anchor's edge it lines up with; `anchor_clicks = true` keeps the anchor clickable while open (a field with suggestions under it) instead of a click on it sending `dismiss` | `open`, `dismiss`, `to`, `side`, `align`, `gap`, `width`, `content`, `keys`, `anchor_clicks` |
| `ui.overlay { ..., content = el }` | content over the whole window: dialogs and palettes (`center`, `top`), sheets (`left`, `right`, `bottom`), toasts (`top-end`, `bottom-end`, ...) | `open`, `dismiss`, `to`, `place`, `backdrop`, `width`, `height`, `keys`, `content` |

**Keys** (`overlay`, `popover`): `keys = { escape = msg, enter = msg, up = msg,
down = msg, ["secondary-k"] = msg }` while it is open and topmost; nothing
else sees those keys. Escape sends `dismiss` unless `keys` names `escape`.
`to = "mod"` sends `dismiss` and `keys` messages to another mod. A click
goes to the innermost clickable element only.
Names are modifiers (`ctrl`, `alt`, `shift`, `cmd`, `secondary` = cmd on
macOS, ctrl elsewhere) then a key, joined by `-`.

### Shared keys

- **Scroll to a child** (`row`, `column`): with `scroll` enabled,
  `scroll_to = 12` reveals direct child 12 (one-based) when the index
  changes. It scrolls only as far as needed and leaves wheel scrolling
  free between changes. Set it to nil to reset the request.

- **Frame keys** (`row`, `column`, `panel`): `grow`, `width`, `height`,
  `gap`, `padding`, `surface`, `border`, `scroll` (`true` along its axis, or `"x"`, `"y"`, `"both"`: code that scrolls sideways), `follow = true` (with `scroll`:
  while at its end, stay there as the content grows, as a chat or log
  does), `shrink = false` (keep
  the content's size instead of being squeezed), `self_align` (`start`,
  `center`, `end`, `stretch`: e.g. keep a capsule at its own width inside a
  column, which otherwise stretches it), `hug = true` (keep its own width in
  a column, and follow a row's `align`: the usual choice for pills, badges
  and dots), `max_width`, `max_height`,
  `float` (out of the flow, over the parent: pinned to an edge or corner,
  `float = "top-right"` (`top-left`, `bottom-left`, `bottom-right`, `top`,
  `bottom`, `left`, `right`, `fill`), set in from it,
  `float = { at = "top-right", inset = 4 }`, or at pixel offsets,
  `float = { top = -4, right = -4 }`, negative overhanging: a count bubble
  on an icon's corner), `area` (out of the flow at fractions of the parent,
  `area = { left = 0.1, top = 0.2, width = 0.5, height = 0.3 }`: a crop
  frame, a marker on a track). `grow` with a `width` or `height` grows from that size.
- **Pointer keys** (`row`, `column`): `pointer = <msg>` is sent as a button
  goes down on it, as the pointer moves while held (anywhere in the
  window), and as it comes up, with `phase` (`down` `move` `up`), `x`, `y`
  (fractions of the box as it was at the press), `dx`, `dy` (pixels since
  the press), `width`, `height`, `button`, `clicks` and the keys held
  (`shift` `alt` `ctrl` `cmd` `secondary`) added. `hover = true` also
  sends `hover` moves and `leave`. `range = { min, max, step, value, speed,
  axis }` adds the `value` a drag sets: where the pointer is between `min`
  and `max` (a slider), or `value` plus pixels times `speed` (a number
  scrubbed by its label). `wheel = <msg>` gets scrolls and pinches (`dx`,
  `dy`, `zoom`, `x`, `y`). On a Mac trackpad, `rotate = <msg>` gets two fingers
  turning (`angle` in degrees clockwise since the last message, `phase`
  `start` `move` `end`), `smart_zoom = <msg>` a two-finger double tap,
  `swipe = <msg>` a finished swipe (`direction` `back` `forward` `up` `down`)
  and `force = <msg>` a force click (`pressure`), each with `x`, `y`;
  `drop = <msg>` gets files dropped from other
  apps (`paths`), which that mod's `ui.image` may then show; `cursor` sets the pointer's
  shape (`crosshair`, `grab`, `grabbing`, `ew-resize`, `ns-resize`,
  `nwse-resize`, `nesw-resize`, `move`, `pointer`, `text`, `not-allowed`).
- **Drag and drop** (`row`, `column`): `carry = <data>` lets the user drag
  it (a card, a row, a calendar event); a box of its size, the `carry`
  rule, follows the pointer while it dims, and a click still clicks.
  `accept = <msg>` on another row or column is sent as it moves over it
  (`phase = "over"`), off it (`"leave"`) and is dropped on it (`"drop"`),
  with `carry` (the data), `from` (the mod that drew it), and `x`, `y`
  (fractions of the target's box: before or after a row's middle) added.
  The innermost target takes the drop; nothing follows a drop, so clear
  what `over` showed then. Other entered targets hear `leave` when the
  drag ends, including cancellation. Not with `pointer` or `drag`.
- **Children:** `false` and `nil` children are skipped, wherever they are.
- **Look keys** (every element but splits): `class = "a b"`,
  `style = { ... }`, and `state = "open"`: a state of the view's own naming,
  which `:open` rules match (`[".drawer:open"] = { width = 280 }`). With a
  `transition` in its rules, a change of state eases colors, opacity,
  width and height from one state's look to the next.
- **Actions:** `msg = <data>` calls the drawing mod's `update` (`to = "name"`
  for another mod or `"provider:<name>"`); `command = "..."` runs an app
  command instead: `quit`, `reload`, `toggle-theme`, `minimize`, `maximize`,
  `close-window`. A browser command (`browser-back`, `browser-forward`,
  `browser-reload`, `browser-stop`, `browser-open`) also takes
  `browser = "<id>"`. To run a command from `update`, without a click, send
  `{ to = "app:command", msg = "minimize" }`.
- **Files:** `{ to = "app:pick", msg = { kind = "open", types = { "tif" },
  multiple = true, reply = "opened" } }` opens the system's panel (`kind`
  `open`, `folder` or `save` with `name` and `folder`); the answer comes
  back to the mod as `reply` with `paths` (`path` for a save) or
  `cancelled = true`. Picked files may then show in that mod's `ui.image`.
- **Text edits:** `{ to = "app:edit", msg = { field = "notes", wrap = {
  "**", "**" } } }` edits the mod's `ui.input` with that `id` around its
  selection, keeping undo and focus: `wrap` puts the two around it (or
  takes them off), `lines = "- "` starts each selected line with it (or
  takes it off), `insert = "@Sam ", back = 3` replaces the selection and
  the 3 bytes before it. A completion can add `at = <caret offset>` and
  `expect = "@sa"`: it applies only with an empty selection there and that
  exact preceding text (`back` must equal its byte length). The field then
  sends its `change`. A toolbar button sends directly (`to = "app:edit"`);
  editing restores focus in the field's own window.
- **Keys anywhere:** `mod { keys = { ["secondary-1"] = "histogram" } }`
  sends its message when the key is pressed and nothing nearer (an open
  overlay, a terminal) took it, to every mod and every mounted copy of
  one (a tab's) that takes it. While a text field has focus it keeps all
  its keys, so mods hear none.
- **Window:** the shell's `mod { window = { titlebar = "hidden",
  traffic_lights = { x, y } } }` draws the layout under the title bar (at
  startup only); `app.window` tells views the `platform`, `titlebar`,
  `maximized`, `fullscreen` and `active`, so a title bar knows whether to
  draw window buttons or leave room for traffic lights.
- **A mod's own window** takes `titlebar = "hidden"` and `traffic_lights`
  in its `window` too, beside `size` and `min_size`, with `drag = true` on
  what moves it. While open, the mod and its instances read that window's
  state as `app.window`; closing it restores the main window's state.
  The mod's view is shared wherever it is mounted.
  `window = "<mod>"` on a row or column opens that
  mod in a window of its own; from `update`, send `{ to = "app:window",
  msg = { open = "<mod>", send = <msg> } }` to open it on a page (`send`
  reaches its `update` first) or `{ close = "<mod>" }` to close it. The
  mod sizes it with `mod { window = { size = { width, height }, min_size
  = { width, height } } }`.
- **Extras** (`row`, `column`, `button`, `item`, `text`, `icon`, `image`,
  `badge`):
  - `tooltip = "text"` shows under the pointer, styled by the `tooltip` rule.
    The rule's `transition` eases it in (`fade`, `slide` rises it a little,
    `slide-fade`), and its delay (`"fade fast 400ms"`, or `delay`) is how
    long the pointer rests before it shows (500ms without one).
  - `context = <data>` is sent on a right-click, to open a context menu
    (to `to = "mod"` if given).
  - `copy = "text"` puts the text on the clipboard when clicked.
- **`ui.memo(key, deps, build)`** returns what `build()` returned the last
  time this view asked for `key` with the same `deps` (a list, compared with
  `==`), or calls it now: for a costly part of a view that depends on a few
  values. A table counts as the same while it is the same table, even if
  changed inside.
- **Views run only when needed:** a view runs again when its state or props
  change (any message to its `update`), when a key of `app` it read
  changes, or on a reload; otherwise its last tree is kept. Read `app.x`
  where you use it rather than copying all of `app`; going through all of
  `app` (`for k, v in app`) runs it on any change.
- **`selected = true`** on a row or column matches `:selected` rules, like an
  item: tabs, segments, chosen tiles.

### Style keys

`background`, `gradient` (`"180deg, #ffa53a, #ff6200"`), `color`, `border`, `border_color`, `radius`, `padding`, `gap`,
`margin`, `shadow`, `size`, `weight` (`light` to `bold`, `semibold` between `medium` and `bold`), `font` (`sans`, `mono`), `case`
(`upper`, `lower`, on text), `opacity`, `width` and `height` (under the
element's own; on containers),
`transition` (a second duration is its delay: `"fade 150ms 40ms"`), `delay`
(replaces the transition's delay, set inline per item to stagger a list),
`clip = true` (hide what overflows the box). Selectors: a part (`row`, `item`, `list`, `popover`, `overlay`, `overlay-backdrop`, `tooltip`, `image`, `markdown`, `markdown-code`, `markdown-quote`, `markdown-alert`, `markdown-find`, `markdown-find-current`, ...),
a class (`.tab`), and a state: `:hover`, `:selected`, `:focus`,
`:disabled`, or one the view names with `state = "..."` (`.drawer:open`).

## Components

Call one with `local name = use "name"`, then `name { ... }` wherever an element goes. Its classes can be restyled in `style.luau`.

| Component | Category | Use it for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`agent-run`](#agent-run) | Agents | Show what an agent started through `app.acp` is doing or did, with Stop and the answers to its permission questions. For the Send feedback dialog, which lists runs with this, use `feedback`; for a chat transcript use `chat-message`. |
| [`feedback`](#feedback) | Agents | Let the user ask for a change to the app itself, from inside it, and follow what the agent does (`app.acp`). For one run on its own use `agent-run`; for a plain form use `dialog`; for chatting with an agent use `composer`. |
| [`accordion`](#accordion) | Containers | A stack of foldable sections of the same kind: a merge request's checks, files and activity, or groups of settings. The mod decides whether opening one closes the others. For one foldable block use `collapsible`; for sidebar groups use `sidebar-section`; for switching between views use `tabs`. |
| [`card`](#card) | Containers | A titled box around related content inside a panel or page; for a whole sidebar section use `ui.panel`, for a plain heading use `section`. |
| [`collapsible`](#collapsible) | Containers | One foldable block of content, such as "No agent yet" or advanced options. For several of them stacked use `accordion`; for a titled sidebar group with a count and actions use `sidebar-section`; for a plain heading use `section`. |
| [`dashboard-card`](#dashboard-card) | Containers | Each block of a dashboard or overview (a chart, a list of things waiting, a table). For a titled box inside a page use `card`; for a sidebar panel use `ui.panel`; for a tiled pane with controls use `pane-frame`. |
| [`section`](#section) | Containers | A small muted heading over a group of content inside a panel or settings page. |
| [`swap-view`](#swap-view) | Containers | The body under a view switcher (`pill-tabs`, `segmented`, `tabs`) whose content is replaced, such as a list's header and rows per filter. Give `width` so the pages can be measured while they move. For panels that open and close use `side-panels`; for items joining a list give the rows a `key` and a transition instead. |
| [`browser`](#browser) | Content | A web page in a pane, with browser chrome. Keep the page's `navigate` messages in state and pass the latest as `page`; the address bar navigates on its own. For a bare page without a bar use `ui.browser`. |
| [`chat-markdown`](#chat-markdown) | Content | A chat answer in markdown, including one still streaming in (pass `cursor` while it grows) or citing its sources with `[label](cite:source)` chips. For a whole document, a note or a README use `markdown` (drawn by the host, with links the mod handles); for a file to edit use `markdown-editor`; for plain text use `ui.text`; for a file's source use `code-view`; for ordered steps alone use `numbered-list`. |
| [`image-viewer`](#image-viewer) | Content | Looking at a picture closely: a scan, a photo, a screenshot, a render, with tools drawn over it (a crop frame, picked spots). The mod keeps `zoom` and `center`. For a picture at a fixed size use `ui.image`; for an avatar use `avatar`. |
| [`markdown`](#markdown) | Content | Show markdown read-only: a README, notes, an agent's answer, release notes written in markdown. For editing a file use `markdown-editor`; for a chat answer streaming in, or one with source chips, use `chat-markdown`; for code alone use `code-view`; for one line of text use `ui.text`. |
| [`markdown-editor`](#markdown-editor) | Content | Editing a markdown file of the project in a tab or a pane. For showing markdown without editing use `markdown`; for code read-only use `code-view`; for a short text field use `ui.input`. |
| [`prose-editor`](#prose-editor) | Content | Writing long text: a draft, an article, notes, a journal, where the words are the whole screen. For a markdown file with a preview beside it use `markdown-editor`; for a short field in a form use `ui.input` (with `multiline` for a text area); for a chat box use `composer`. |
| [`video-viewer`](#video-viewer) | Content | Previewing a camera or scanner, or inspecting a full-resolution frame, with an engine writing a frame ring (`ui.video`). The mod keeps `zoom` and `center`. For a picture in a file use `image-viewer`. |
| [`button-group`](#button-group) | Controls | Related actions or view modes side by side in a header: Unified \| Split, Uncommitted \| Branch, zoom − \| +. For a settings choice in a track use `segmented`; for separate quiet buttons use `toolbar`; for back/forward use `nav-buttons`. |
| [`caffeine`](#caffeine) | Controls | A scan, render or copy that runs unattended: put it in a status bar or toolbar for the user to turn on. A mod that knows when its job starts and ends should send `app:awake` itself instead. |
| [`chips`](#chips) | Controls | Filters over a list where any number can be on (Open, Mine, Has agent). For exactly one of a few use `segmented`; for read-only labels use `tags`; for a single on/off setting use `switch`. |
| [`copy-field`](#copy-field) | Controls | Text the user will paste elsewhere: an install command, a token, a URL, a path. For read-only label/value pairs use `key-values`; for an editable field wait for `ui.input`. |
| [`dropdown`](#dropdown) | Controls | Pick one of many options that do not fit a `segmented` control (more than 3 or 4, or long labels), or a button that opens a menu of actions. For 2 to 4 short choices use `segmented`; for a menu on right-click use `context-menu`; for the menu rows alone use `menu`. |
| [`filter-dropdown`](#filter-dropdown) | Controls | Filters in a row over a table or list (activity type, author, date range), each narrowing it to one or a few values. For toggles that are each on or off use `chips`; for a setting rather than a filter use `dropdown`; for a free-text filter use `search-field`. |
| [`icon-button`](#icon-button) | Controls | An action or toggle shown only as an icon: in a title bar, a panel header, a toolbar. Always give a `tooltip`. For buttons with words use `ui.button` or `toolbar`; for back/forward use `nav-buttons`; for joined icon choices use `button-group`. |
| [`picker`](#picker) | Controls | A property of a record set from many options: assignee, labels, project, status, priority, "blocked by", in a task's detail panel or a row. For a setting in a form use `dropdown`; for a filter over a list use `filter-dropdown`; for 2 to 4 short choices use `segmented`; for addresses use `recipient-field`. |
| [`segmented`](#segmented) | Controls | A setting with 2 to 4 short, mutually exclusive values (Light / Dark / System, All / Mine). For more or longer options use `dropdown`; for a vertical list with descriptions use `radio-group`; for switching documents or views use `tabs`; for actions rather than a choice use `button-group`. |
| [`toolbar`](#toolbar) | Controls | A row of small quiet buttons above a panel or list. For icon-only buttons use `icon-button`; for one-of-many choices use `segmented`. |
| [`audio-meter`](#audio-meter) | Data | Sound levels while recording or playing, from values an engine published. For a fraction that isn't sound use `vertical-bar` or `meter`. |
| [`avatar`](#avatar) | Data | Stand for a person, space, project or agent by its name: comment authors, workspace switchers, people lists. Use `comment-card` for an authored message (it draws one), `status-dot` for a state alone. |
| [`avatar-stack`](#avatar-stack) | Data | Who is in a group, in a card or a row (38 investors, 3 reviewers), when their names matter less than how many. For one person use `avatar`; for a list of people use `list` or `table`. |
| [`bar-chart`](#bar-chart) | Data | Counts over time or per category: tokens per day, runs per hour, alerts per device, stacked by kind. For a tiny live trend in a status bar use `sparkline`; for one fraction use `meter`; for one headline number use `stat-tile`. |
| [`chat-message`](#chat-message) | Data | Each turn of a conversation with an agent or a person, stacked in a scrolling column over a `composer`. For a comment on a pull request use `comment-card`; for a notification use `toast`. |
| [`code-view`](#code-view) | Data | Show code or a log read-only: a file at a line, a snippet in a comment, a test's output. For changes use `diff-view`; for a live shell use `terminal`. |
| [`comment-card`](#comment-card) | Data | Comments in a pull request conversation, review threads, notes left by agents or people. Stack them in a column. For a numbered review note with a remove button use `note-card`; for events in order use `timeline`. |
| [`contribution-graph`](#contribution-graph) | Data | Daily activity over months or a year, GitHub style: commits, agent runs, posts, workouts, a streak. Pass one count per day and the first day's date. For weekly or arbitrary buckets without dates use `heat-grid`; for counts with an axis use `bar-chart`; for picking a day use `month-grid`. |
| [`count-bubble`](#count-bubble) | Data | An unread or pending count on a sidebar icon, a tab or a menu entry; pass `float = { top = -4, right = -4 }` to put it on the corner of its parent. For a status use `status-dot`; for a text label use `ui.badge`; for added/removed lines use `diff-counts`. |
| [`country-code`](#country-code) | Data | Beside a country's name in lists of locations or settings, in place of a flag (no flag images ship). For any short label use `ui.badge` or `pill`. |
| [`course-card`](#course-card) | Data | The one course, plan or program a page puts first, with where the reader is and a button to carry on. For a grid of guides use `guide-card`; for a figure with a trend use `stat-tile`; for a titled box of anything use `card`. |
| [`date-tile`](#date-tile) | Data | Beside dated items in a list (deadlines, calls, distributions, events) where the date leads. For a date inside a line of text use plain text; for picking a day use `day-strip` or `month-grid`. |
| [`document-card`](#document-card) | Data | A home screen or a folder of notes shown as a grid. For a list beside an editor use `document-row`; for attached files use `file-card`; for reading material with progress use `guide-card`. |
| [`dot-chart`](#dot-chart) | Data | A daily or weekly count compared with the period before (signups, orders), where the squares' rhythm reads better than smooth bars. For stacked counts by kind use `bar-chart`; for a balance against a floor use `forecast-chart`; for a trend line use `ui.line`. |
| [`file-card`](#file-card) | Data | Attachments on a task, a comment or a message, in a grid of tiles or a list of rows, while they upload and after. For the area files are dropped on use `dropzone`; for a file in a tree use `tree` with `file-icon`; for a picture to look at closely use `image-viewer`. |
| [`file-icon`](#file-icon) | Data | Beside a file name in a tree, a tab or a list of changes. For a generic icon use `ui.icon`. |
| [`forecast-chart`](#forecast-chart) | Data | A balance or capacity projected over weeks or months against a minimum (cash against a floor, stock against a reorder point). For counts per bucket, stacked by kind, use `bar-chart`; for a small trend use `sparkline` or `ui.line`. |
| [`gantt`](#gantt) | Data | A project's schedule or timeline: when tasks run, how far they are, what waits on what. For events placed in hours use `week-calendar`; for a dated list of events use `timeline`; for a board by status use `kanban-column`. |
| [`guide-card`](#guide-card) | Data | Cards of reading material or courses the reader works through (guides, docs, tutorials), three or so to a row, each with how far the reader got. For one featured course with actions use `course-card`; for a plain titled box use `card`; for a linked record inside a message use `record-card`. |
| [`heat-grid`](#heat-grid) | Data | Activity over days or weeks at a glance: lessons per week, posts per day, a streak, a course's progress as squares. For a GitHub-style calendar of days with months and weekdays use `contribution-graph`; for a count compared with the period before use `dot-chart`; for stacked counts with an axis use `bar-chart`; for one fraction use `meter` or `progress`. |
| [`histogram`](#histogram) | Data | The spread of a picture's tones (red, green, blue, luminance), of latencies or of scores, where the shape matters more than any count; with draggable markers it is a levels control. For counts per labelled bucket use `bar-chart`; for a trend over time use `ui.line` or `series-chart`. |
| [`kbd`](#kbd) | Data | Show a keyboard shortcut: in a menu row, a palette result, a tooltip line or a help sheet. Inside menus `menu` already draws one from an item's `shortcut`; for a word-like tag use `ui.badge`. |
| [`key-values`](#key-values) | Data | Read-only properties or details: aligned label/value lines. For editable settings use `settings-row`. |
| [`kpi-cell`](#kpi-cell) | Data | A row of three to five headline figures across the top of a dashboard (readers, signups, churn), set side by side in a bordered strip. For a figure inside a card's text use `metric`; for a standalone tile with a sparkline use `stat-tile`. |
| [`kpi-meter`](#kpi-meter) | Data | A strip of headline figures where each one is a part of a whole (on time / late, fixed / open, one segment per notice). For a figure with a change pill use `kpi-cell`; for one fraction use `meter`; for a whole split into labelled parts in a card use `share-bar`. |
| [`line-chart`](#line-chart) | Data | A measure over days or weeks compared with a forecast or a target (actual against predicted, this year against last), where the user picks a day to read its figures. For several readings on one scale with a legend and a crosshair use `series-chart`; for bars against a floor use `forecast-chart`; for stacked counts use `bar-chart`; for a bare trend use `ui.line` or `sparkline`. |
| [`message-header`](#message-header) | Data | Above the body of an email or a thread's message in a reading pane. For a row in the message list use `mail-row`; for a comment in a review use `comment-card`; for a chat turn use `chat-message`. |
| [`meter`](#meter) | Data | A fraction (0 to 1) as a bar with its percentage: memory, quota, progress of a known size. For work with no known size use `progress` with `busy`; for a narrow upright bar in a tight row use `vertical-bar`. |
| [`metric`](#metric) | Data | Headline figures across the top of a dashboard card: cash today, the lowest week, a total. For a figure in its own tile with a trend use `stat-tile`; for a status bar reading use `stat`; for a fraction use `meter`. |
| [`mini-bars`](#mini-bars) | Data | A figure over a few periods in a KPI strip or a card header (revenue by month, signups by week). For a live trend in a status bar use `sparkline`; for a full chart with an axis use `bar-chart` or `forecast-chart`. |
| [`note-card`](#note-card) | Data | Notes a person leaves on lines while reviewing, to send to an agent; list them in a column beside a `diff-view`. For an authored comment use `comment-card`. |
| [`numbered-list`](#numbered-list) | Data | Ordered steps or suggestions in a message, a note or a help page. For a checklist use `task-row`; for events in time use `timeline`. |
| [`pill`](#pill) | Data | A tag on a row ("Work", "Health") or a count inside a sentence ("2 events"), where colour carries meaning. For several read-only labels use `tags`; for filters the user toggles use `chips`; for a plain status word use `ui.badge`. |
| [`pixel-icon`](#pixel-icon) | Data | A playful, recognisable mark for an agent, a bot, a project or a workspace, at any size from a list row (18 px) to a header (64 px). For a person's initial use `avatar`; for a generic glyph use `ui.icon`. |
| [`priority-icon`](#priority-icon) | Data | Beside a task's title in a list, a board card or a detail panel, and in the menu that changes it. For a task's status use `status-icon`; for a coloured label use `pill`. |
| [`progress`](#progress) | Data | Progress of a task: a download, an index, a build step. Use `busy = true` when the size is unknown. For a reading such as memory use `meter`; for a quota with a reset use `usage-bar`; for a spinner alone use `ui.icon { name = "loader-circle", spin = true }`. |
| [`progress-stack`](#progress-stack) | Data | How far a goal is (a raise, a budget, a quota) split by stage: closed, out, soft, still needed, with where the pace leads. For one fraction use `meter`; for a quota with a reset use `usage-bar`; for task progress use `progress`. |
| [`project-card`](#project-card) | Data | The projects page of a task manager, two to four cards to a row, each opening its project. For one project's row in a list use `list` or `table`; for a card on a board use `board-card`; for reading material use `guide-card`. |
| [`record-card`](#record-card) | Data | A record an agent or a person points at inside a message or a note, which a click opens. For a full row in a list use `list` or `pr-row`; for a dated item use `date-tile` beside text. |
| [`relative-time`](#relative-time) | Data | An age or last-updated time in rows, cards and headers. Pass elapsed `seconds`: the mod computes them from a provider's timestamp and the current time. Use `compact` in tight columns (PR lists, tables). For a dated list of events use `timeline`. |
| [`rich-text`](#rich-text) | Data | A sentence that mixes emphasis and labels in one line: an audit log's activity, a notification, a table cell ("Order #1213 marked as [Fulfilled]"). For a paragraph use `ui.text`; for a lone label use `pill` or `ui.badge`; for several labels use `tags`. |
| [`route-map`](#route-map) | Data | Where a day's meetings are, a delivery round, a trip: places in order and the way between them. For one place without a route, `ui.map` with a pin is enough. |
| [`series-chart`](#series-chart) | Data | Several readings over the same period compared on one scale (CPU, GPU and memory over 24 hours; requests and errors by hour), where the reader wants a sample's exact values. For counts stacked per bucket use `bar-chart`; for periods against a forecast with a picked day's card use `line-chart`; for one small trend use `ui.line` or `sparkline`; for a balance against a floor use `forecast-chart`. |
| [`share-bar`](#share-bar) | Data | How a whole splits into a few parts, above a list of those parts (devices, engagement tiers, plans). For progress toward a target with stages use `progress-stack`; for one fraction use `meter`. |
| [`sparkline`](#sparkline) | Data | Recent samples as tiny bars, like CPU over the last minute, in a status bar or header. For the latest sample alone in a tight row use `vertical-bar`. |
| [`spotlight-bars`](#spotlight-bars) | Data | One figure over a dozen periods where one period is the story (revenue by month, the best week), in a dashboard card that is wide and tall. For several series stacked use `bar-chart`; for a few small bars in a KPI strip use `mini-bars`; for a balance against a floor use `forecast-chart`. |
| [`spreadsheet`](#spreadsheet) | Data | Data laid out as a spreadsheet the user (or an agent) fills cell by cell: research sheets, imports, editable records, with cells still loading shown as skeleton bars. For a read-only list of records with sorting use `table`; for label/value pairs use `key-values`. |
| [`stat-tile`](#stat-tile) | Data | A headline number on a dashboard or overview: open PRs, tokens today, uptime, failing checks; put several in a wrapping row. For a status bar reading use `stat`; for a fraction use `meter`; for a quota use `usage-bar`; for a series use `bar-chart`. |
| [`status-icon`](#status-icon) | Data | Beside a task's title in a list, a board card or a detail panel, and in the menu that changes it. For an agent's or job's state use `status-dot`; for a check the user ticks use `task-check`; for a priority use `priority-icon`. |
| [`system-load`](#system-load) | Data | CPU and memory of a machine in a status bar, a host row of a sidebar, or a card header. Use `compact` beside a name in a tight row. For one reading alone use `sparkline`, `meter` or `vertical-bar`. |
| [`table`](#table) | Data | Tabular data with several aligned fields per row: devices, processes, files, runs; an admin list (audit log, orders) as `bordered` and `checkable`, with `filter-dropdown`s over it and `pagination` under it. For one field per row use `list`; for pull requests use `pr-row`; for label/value pairs use `key-values`. |
| [`tags`](#tags) | Data | A wrapping set of small labels: languages, topics, states. |
| [`threshold-line`](#threshold-line) | Data | A metric against its target or limit in a dashboard card: % within SLA against 95%, latency against 2s, lag against 5 minutes. For a line without a target use `ui.line`; for tiny bars use `sparkline`; for bars against a floor use `forecast-chart`. |
| [`tick-meter`](#tick-meter) | Data | A resource's utilization in a dense, technical dashboard (CPU, GPU, memory, a queue's depth), where a striped instrument reads better than a smooth bar. For a compact bar with its percentage use `meter`; for a quota with a reset use `usage-bar`; for task progress use `progress`. |
| [`timeline`](#timeline) | Data | Events in order: checkpoints, commits, deploys, an agent's steps. For a flat selectable list use `list`; for comments use `comment-card`; for a table of runs use `table`. |
| [`usage-bar`](#usage-bar) | Data | A rate limit or quota with a reset (an AI plan's weekly or 5-hour window, an API budget), in a usage sheet or settings page. For a plain fraction use `meter`; for task progress use `progress`; for a single big number use `stat-tile`. |
| [`vectorscope`](#vectorscope) | Data | Judging colour balance and saturation from points an engine measured and published (up to 480, thinned out; more are left out). For levels across the picture use `waveform`; for tones use `histogram`. |
| [`vertical-bar`](#vertical-bar) | Data | A fraction in a row with no room for a horizontal bar: a host's CPU or memory beside its name in a sidebar, a queue's depth in a tab. For a bar with room to spread use `meter`; for a history use `sparkline`. |
| [`waveform`](#waveform) | Data | Setting exposure or light against a picture's levels, from values an engine measured and published (a few hundred columns). For the spread of tones with no position use `histogram`; for hue and saturation use `vectorscope`. |
| [`week-calendar`](#week-calendar) | Data | Meetings, bookings or shifts placed in time: a day or week of hours where events span their length and overlapping ones share the column, or a month of them. For picking a day without events use `month-grid` or `day-strip`; for events in order without hours use `timeline`; for a day's list use `task-row`. |
| [`banner`](#banner) | Feedback | A message across the whole window or pane that stays until dealt with: the current worktree's branch, a failed provider, an update ready. For a transient message use a toast (`ui.overlay` at `bottom-end`); for a status inside a row use `status-dot` or `ui.badge`; for an empty pane use `empty-state`. |
| [`empty-state`](#empty-state) | Feedback | A list, panel or page with nothing to show yet, optionally with one action to fix that. For loading use `loading-row`; for failures use `notice`. |
| [`error-state`](#error-state) | Feedback | In place of content that failed to load (a list, a pane, a provider's data). For an in-page warning that isn't a failed load use `notice`; for a lost daemon or SSH connection use `reconnecting`; for nothing to show use `empty-state`; for a transient failure use `toast`. |
| [`insight-note`](#insight-note) | Feedback | An assistant's finding beside the data it explains (under a chart, over a table, in a checklist card). For a warning that must be dealt with use `notice`; for a conversation use `chat-message`; for a transient message use `toast`. |
| [`key-hints`](#key-hints) | Feedback | Under a palette, picker, list or dialog to say which keys work there. For a full reference of shortcuts use `shortcuts`; for one shortcut beside a menu item or button use `kbd`. |
| [`loading`](#loading) | Feedback | While data loads: inline beside a label, centred in an empty pane (`block`), or as `skeleton` bars where rows will appear. For known progress use `progress`; for a lost connection use `reconnecting`; for a failure use `error-state`; for nothing to show use `empty-state`. |
| [`notice`](#notice) | Feedback | A message that belongs in the page and stays until handled: a config error, an announcement, a permission problem. For transient notifications use `toast`/`toasts`; for a failed load with Retry use `error-state`; for an empty list use `empty-state`. |
| [`reconnecting`](#reconnecting) | Feedback | A whole window or pane depends on a connection that dropped (the daemon, an SSH host, a cloud machine) and must wait for it. For a failed load inside one pane use `error-state`; for a brief note that something reconnected use `toast`; for plain loading use `loading`. |
| [`release-notes`](#release-notes) | Feedback | A What's new page, an update panel or a changelog list (one per release, older ones `collapsed`). For the update offer itself use `update-pill`; for a first-run tour use `onboarding`; for a dated activity feed use `timeline`. |
| [`thinking`](#thinking) | Feedback | Inside an agent's `chat-message`, before its answer. For a spinner while it is still thinking use `loading`; for a general fold use `collapsible`. |
| [`toast`](#toast) | Feedback | A single transient notification, usually inside `toasts`, which stacks them in a window corner. For a message that stays in the page use `notice`; for a blocking question use `confirm`; for an app update use `update-pill`. |
| [`toasts`](#toasts) | Feedback | The app's notifications: keep a list in the mod's state, push to it, remove on `dismiss` (or after a timer). For one card inline use `toast`; for a persistent callout in a page use `notice`; for an update offer use `update-pill`. |
| [`update-pill`](#update-pill) | Feedback | Tell the user an update is downloaded and ready to install, without interrupting. For the changelog itself use `release-notes`; for other notifications use `toast`/`toasts`; for a lasting in-page message use `notice`. |
| [`checkbox`](#checkbox) | Forms | An option that is on or off among others in a form or list, or a "select all" (indeterminate when some are). For a setting that applies at once use `switch`; for one of many use `radio-group`; for filter toggles use `chips`. |
| [`choice-cards`](#choice-cards) | Forms | Pick one of several options that are best seen: a theme, a layout, a template, an agent. For short text options use `segmented` or `radio-group`; for a colour use `swatches`; for a menu use `dropdown`. |
| [`composer`](#composer) | Forms | The bottom of a chat with an agent or a person. For a search box use `search-field`; for a longer form field use `ui.input` with `multiline`. |
| [`curve-editor`](#curve-editor) | Forms | A tone or response curve the user shapes by hand: a photo's gradation curve per channel, an easing, a gain curve. For one value along a range use `slider`; for a fixed set of levels over a histogram use `histogram` with markers. |
| [`date-picker`](#date-picker) | Forms | Setting a date on a record: a task's due date, a start date, a reminder, with presets for the usual ones. For the grid alone (a calendar view) use `month-grid`; for a time of day use `time-picker`; for a strip of days over a list use `day-strip`. |
| [`dictation`](#dictation) | Forms | Let the user talk instead of type: beside a prompt, in `composer`'s `actions`. The drawing mod must be in `recorders` of providers/speech. Give it `listening`, and send `provider:speech` `{ cancel = true }` if it stops being drawn while listening (a closing dialog), or the microphone stays on until the limit. |
| [`dropzone`](#dropzone) | Forms | Adding attachments to a task, a message or a form: files dragged from other apps land on it, and browse opens the system's file panel (`{ to = "app:pick", ... }`). Show what was added under it with `file-card`. For a button alone use `ui.button`; for an empty list with one action use `empty-state`. |
| [`filter-builder`](#filter-builder) | Forms | Filtering a list or board by conditions the user builds (status is Done, assignee is not Sarah), inside a `ui.popover` under a Filter button. For one filter per chip over a table use `filter-dropdown`; for toggles use `chips`; for a text query use `search-field`. |
| [`find-bar`](#find-bar) | Forms | Finding text in the document or pane on screen (⌘F). For filtering a list use `search-field`; for running commands use `command-palette`. |
| [`form-grid`](#form-grid) | Forms | A dense form in a tool's sidebar or inspector: an output's size, a scanner's holder, a file name. For a settings page with descriptions use `settings-row`; for read-only label/value pairs use `key-values`. |
| [`mention-field`](#mention-field) | Forms | A comment box, a task's description or a chat message where people are mentioned. For addresses on a message use `recipient-field`; for a chat with an agent use `composer`; for a plain field use `ui.input`. |
| [`number-field`](#number-field) | Forms | A number the user sets exactly or nudges: a resolution, a frame number, a zoom, a count, in a dense settings form or inspector. Read `tonumber(msg.value)` for both typing and dragging. For a value along a range where the feel matters use `slider`; for a small count with buttons only use `stepper`. |
| [`radio-group`](#radio-group) | Forms | Pick one of a few options that need a description or room to read (a mode, a policy). For 2 to 4 short values use `segmented`; for many values use `dropdown`; for options with a picture use `choice-cards`; for independent on/off options use `checkbox`. |
| [`recipient-field`](#recipient-field) | Forms | The To, Cc and Bcc lines of a message being written, or inviting people by address. For tags the user only reads use `tags`; for filters use `chips`; for a single free-text value use `ui.input`; for a search box use `search-field`. |
| [`search-field`](#search-field) | Forms | A query box over a list or palette: filter files, branches or commands as the user types, with up and down to move through results. For a longer value use `ui.input` (multiline for a text area); for one-of-many choices use `segmented` or `dropdown`. |
| [`selection-toolbar`](#selection-toolbar) | Forms | A `ui.input` or `prose-editor` that keeps its chrome out of the way until words are selected. For a bar that always shows use `text-editor`; for actions on a row use `context-menu`. |
| [`settings-row`](#settings-row) | Forms | Each line of a settings page or preferences card, holding a `switch`, `segmented`, `dropdown` or button. Group rows under `settings-page` sections; for read-only properties use `key-values`; for a labelled switch on its own use `switch` with `label`. |
| [`shortcut-field`](#shortcut-field) | Forms | Letting the user rebind a shortcut, in a `settings-row` or a `shortcuts` page. For showing a shortcut use `kbd`; for a list of them use `shortcuts`. |
| [`slider`](#slider) | Forms | A setting along a continuous range where the feel matters more than the exact number: contrast, saturation, an amount, a radius, a volume. For a number the user types or nudges use `number-field` or `stepper`; for a fraction shown read-only use `meter`; for a few named values use `segmented`. |
| [`stepper`](#stepper) | Forms | A small number nudged up or down: a font size, a column count, a delay. For a fraction shown as a bar use `meter`; for one of a few named sizes use `segmented`. |
| [`swatches`](#swatches) | Forms | Pick a colour from a short palette: a workspace or tag colour, an accent. For themes (many colours each) use `choice-cards` with a swatch row as the preview; to show colours without picking, use `ui.row`s with a background. |
| [`switch`](#switch) | Forms | A setting that takes effect at once, on or off ("High contrast"). For a choice that is confirmed later or part of a list of options use `checkbox`; for one of several values use `segmented` or `radio-group`. |
| [`task-check`](#task-check) | Forms | The check at the start of a task or to-do row; a click sends `msg` for the mod to flip it. For a form option use `checkbox`; for an agent's state use `status-dot`. |
| [`text-editor`](#text-editor) | Forms | A task's or project's description, release notes, a long comment: text with some formatting, edited in place. For a markdown file of the project use `markdown-editor`; for markdown only shown use `markdown`; for a chat message use `composer`; for one line use `ui.input`. |
| [`time-picker`](#time-picker) | Forms | Choosing when: Send Later, Snooze or a reminder's "Choose a Time…", beside a `month-grid` for the day. For a list of preset moments alone use `menu` or `dropdown`; for a number that is not a time use `stepper`; for a day use `month-grid` or `day-strip`. |
| [`ahead-behind`](#ahead-behind) | Git | A branch's sync state beside its name: sidebars, title bars, branch lists. For lines changed use `diff-counts`. |
| [`change-tree`](#change-tree) | Git | The changed files of a repository or a review, as the right pane's Changes shows `app.git.files`. For every file in a folder use `tree`; for a file's lines use `diff-view`. |
| [`checks`](#checks) | Git | CI runs or readiness factors for a pull request or branch: a PR detail pane, a merge dialog. For a single summary dot use `pr-badge` or `pr-row` with `checks`; for an agent's state use `status-dot`. |
| [`diff-counts`](#diff-counts) | Git | The size of a change beside a file, commit, branch or PR: file lists, rows, title bars. For commits ahead and behind use `ahead-behind`; for a whole diff use `diff-view`. |
| [`diff-view`](#diff-view) | Git | Show a file's changes for review: a review pane, a checkpoint, a commit. Stack one per file in a scrolling column. For only the size of a change use `diff-counts`; for a file without changes use `code-view`. |
| [`forge-account`](#forge-account) | Git | The account control beside `forge-pr` in a title bar or sidebar footer. What the click opens is the app's: show `forge-sign-in` in a `dialog` or a popover, or a settings page of your own. |
| [`forge-pr`](#forge-pr) | Git | Wherever a branch shows its pull request: the title bar (the current branch, falling back to uncommitted lines), beside each worktree or branch in a sidebar (`branch = worktree.branch`). It reads the forge provider's data; for a number you already have use `pr-badge`, for a whole list row `pr-row`. |
| [`forge-sign-in`](#forge-sign-in) | Git | The body of the app's own sign-in, opened from `forge-account` or a settings page. Draw your own instead from `app.github.auth` when it should look different; send the provider the same messages. |
| [`pr-badge`](#pr-badge) | Git | A pull or merge request referenced inline: beside a branch in a sidebar, in a title bar, in a tab. For a full list row use `pr-row`; for CI details use `checks`; for an agent's state use `status-dot`. |
| [`pr-row`](#pr-row) | Git | Lists of pull requests, merge requests or issues, as in an orchestrator or review queue; stack rows in a scrolling column, under `section` headings per group. For a PR referenced inline use `pr-badge`; for a generic data grid use `table`; for its CI use `checks`. |
| [`mockups`](#mockups) | Layout | Showing the user a few ideas for a change before making it, so they can pick one: the moonframe-mockups skill builds a throwaway mod around it. Not for real content; for choosing between options inside the app use `choice-cards`. |
| [`page`](#page) | Layout | The main area of a settings screen, a detail view or a dashboard: a big title, then sections of content that scroll. Group its content with `section` or `card`; put it beside a `sidebar` in a `split-view`. For a framed pane use `pane-frame`; for a modal use `dialog`; for a panel in a sidebar use `ui.panel`. |
| [`pane-frame`](#pane-frame) | Layout | Framing each pane of a tiled workspace (a terminal, an agent, a log) with its own header and controls. The panes' sizes come from `ui.hsplit`/`ui.vsplit` (see `split-view`); this only draws the frame inside one. For a titled box of content use `card`; for a sidebar panel use `ui.panel`. |
| [`settings-page`](#settings-page) | Layout | A whole preferences window or settings tab. It is made of `settings-nav` (the page list) and `settings-row` (each setting); use those directly for a different arrangement, `section` for a plain heading, `card` to box a group. |
| [`side-panels`](#side-panels) | Layout | A three-column app (notes, mail, writing) whose sidebar and list the user hides to focus on the main area. The mod keeps `left` and `middle` and flips them from buttons in the panes' headers. For resizable panes, an inspector or a bottom panel use `split-view`; for a switcher over the list use `pill-tabs`. |
| [`split-view`](#split-view) | Layout | The body of a shell or a large mod: a sidebar, the main content and optional inspector and bottom panes the user can resize and toggle. It is plain `ui.hsplit`/`ui.vsplit` with `ui.pane` children; write those directly for any other arrangement. For framing each pane use `pane-frame`; for a scrolling page inside the main area use `page`. |
| [`board-card`](#board-card) | Lists | Items in a `kanban-column`: deals, tickets, tasks, candidates. For a row in a list use `task-row` or `list`; for a pull request use `pr-row`. |
| [`document-row`](#document-row) | Lists | The list of documents in a writing or notes app (drafts, articles, notes), stacked in a scrolling column beside the editor. For mail use `mail-row`; for tasks use `task-row`; for files in folders use `tree` or `file-tree`; for a plain row use `list`. |
| [`group-header`](#group-header) | Lists | A heading inside a list that groups its rows by state or owner ("Needs you 3", "Waiting 3", a machine with its online dot). For a sidebar's own sections use `sidebar-section`; for a heading over arbitrary content use `section`; for nested rows use `tree`. |
| [`kanban-column`](#kanban-column) | Lists | Each stage of a kanban board (deals, tickets, tasks by status); put several in a row that scrolls sideways and fill them with `board-card`. For a list grouped by status without columns use `group-header` over rows. |
| [`level-row`](#level-row) | Lists | Rows of a breakdown where each part is read on its own scale: leads by status, a funnel's stages, tickets by priority. For parts of one whole with shares use `ratio-row` or `share-bar`; for one fraction with a percentage use `meter`; for a quota use `usage-bar`. |
| [`list`](#list) | Lists | A plain selectable list of rows with label, detail and badge. For rich rows (status, icons, two lines) use `agent-row`, `workspace-row` or `tree`. |
| [`mail-row`](#mail-row) | Lists | Each row of an inbox or a mailbox's message list; stack them in a `ui.list` (rows of one height) or a scrolling column, under `segmented` category tabs. For tasks use `task-row`; for pull requests use `pr-row`; for a plain selectable row use `list`; for the open message's header use `message-header`. |
| [`ratio-row`](#ratio-row) | Lists | Lists of parts of a whole: where signups came from, top countries, devices, tiers. Stack them in a column; give `share` for the bar under each. For a bar of all the parts at once use `share-bar`; for a data grid use `table`. |
| [`task-row`](#task-row) | Lists | Rows of tasks, to-dos, habits or events in a planner, an inbox or a day view; stack them in a column under `section` headings. For a plain selectable row use `list`; for pull requests use `pr-row`. |
| [`tree`](#tree) | Lists | Nested rows: a file tree in a review, worktrees under a repository, agents and their sub-agents. For flat rows use `list`; for a heading over a group of rows use `group-header`; for one foldable block use `collapsible`. |
| [`activity-bar`](#activity-bar) | Navigation | Switching between the app's main views from a thin strip at the window's edge (terminals, pull requests, issues, agents, settings). For a collapsed list of workspaces use `rail`; for text tabs use `tabs`; for a full list of rows use `sidebar`. |
| [`breadcrumbs`](#breadcrumbs) | Navigation | Where a detail view sits in a hierarchy (repository › Pull requests › !2), with a way back up and to step through siblings. For a window's top row use `title-bar`; for switching views use `tabs`; for a pane's own header use `pane-frame`. |
| [`day-strip`](#day-strip) | Navigation | Picking a day in a planner, an agenda or a log, over the list for that day. For a whole month use a calendar grid; for steps of a flow use `pager`; for a few named views use `segmented`. |
| [`month-grid`](#month-grid) | Navigation | A calendar view or a date picker's body: choosing a day in a month. For a strip of days over a list use `day-strip`; for events in order use `timeline`. |
| [`nav-buttons`](#nav-buttons) | Navigation | History navigation in a title bar, a browser tab or a pane that keeps a back stack. For onboarding steps use `pager`; for a single icon action use `icon-button`. |
| [`outline`](#outline) | Navigation | Beside a long document: a README, a note, a report read in a `markdown`. For a file tree use `tree`; for an app's navigation use `side-nav`; for steps use `numbered-list`. |
| [`pager`](#pager) | Navigation | Steps of an onboarding or welcome flow, or pages of a carousel. For history back/forward use `nav-buttons`; for switching views use `tabs` or `segmented`. |
| [`pagination`](#pagination) | Navigation | Under a table or list too long to show at once (an audit log, orders, invoices), when the user steps through it by page. For a list that scrolls use `ui.list`; for steps of an onboarding flow use `pager`; for history use `nav-buttons`. |
| [`pill-tabs`](#pill-tabs) | Navigation | Switching the few views of one list from a sidebar or header (Inbox, All, Last 7 Days), where the current view deserves its name and the rest only an icon. For settings choices use `segmented`; for documents or sessions use `tabs`; for the app's main views use `activity-bar`. |
| [`rail`](#rail) | Navigation | The sidebar folded to a narrow strip, one tile per workspace or agent with its status. For switching the app's views use `activity-bar`; for the full width version use `sidebar`. |
| [`settings-nav`](#settings-nav) | Navigation | Choosing the page of a settings or preferences window; pair it with `settings-page`, which uses it. For an app's main sidebar use `sidebar`; for a flat list use `list`; for tabs across the top use `tabs`. |
| [`side-nav`](#side-nav) | Navigation | An app's main navigation that the user folds to icons and back (mail folders, views, projects, threads), with an account header and counts. For workspace tiles with status use `rail` beside a `sidebar`; for foldable groups of arbitrary rows use `sidebar`; for a VS Code strip beside a panel use `activity-bar`. |
| [`sidebar`](#sidebar) | Navigation | The whole left column of an app: workspaces, agents, settings categories. One group alone is `sidebar-section`; the narrow collapsed form is `rail`; a VS Code style icon strip beside it is `activity-bar`; nested rows are `tree`. |
| [`sidebar-section`](#sidebar-section) | Navigation | A titled group of rows inside a sidebar ("Spaces", "Agents", "APPEARANCE"). The whole column is `sidebar`; a list heading with a status dot and `+` is `group-header`; a foldable card in a page is `collapsible`; a plain non-folding heading is `section`. |
| [`tab-view`](#tab-view) | Navigation | Drawing the selected tab of a `tabbed` bar somewhere other than under it, from the `tabs/<id>` topic. `tabbed` uses it for its own content. |
| [`tabbed`](#tabbed) | Navigation | Several terminals, browsers or tools in one place, opened and closed by the user, remembered across launches. For a strip whose tabs the mod keeps itself use `tabs`. |
| [`tabs`](#tabs) | Navigation | Switch between open documents, terminals or agent sessions, or between views of one panel. For 2 to 4 settings choices use `segmented`; for joined action buttons use `button-group`; for onboarding steps use `pager`. |
| [`title-bar`](#title-bar) | Navigation | The top row of a window whose shell sets `titlebar = "hidden"`: pass `window = app.window` and it leaves room for macOS's traffic lights or draws its own window buttons elsewhere. Put `tabs` in its content. For a bar along the bottom use `status-bar`; for a path inside a pane use `breadcrumbs`; for a plain row of buttons use `toolbar`. |
| [`about`](#about) | Overlays | Help > About, or the top of a settings General page (`inline`). For the changes in a version use `release-notes`; for other properties use `key-values`; for a first-run welcome use `onboarding`. |
| [`action-tiles`](#action-tiles) | Overlays | The menu a workspace, worktree or agent opens on click, when its few main actions deserve big targets (new worktree, fan out, rename, close). Wrap it in `ui.popover`. For a plain list of commands use `menu` or `context-menu`; for a yes/no question use `confirm`; for picking one of several options use `choice-cards`. |
| [`command-palette`](#command-palette) | Overlays | Run any of the app's or a mod's commands from the keyboard (⌘K, ⌘⇧P), or jump to a file, branch or workspace by name. For a menu under a button use `dropdown`; for right-click actions use `context-menu`; for a list of shortcuts to read use `shortcuts`; for a search box over a list in a pane use `search-field`. |
| [`confirm`](#confirm) | Overlays | Ask before doing something, especially destructive (close a window with running agents, delete a branch). For a modal with a form or custom body use `dialog`; for an undo-able action prefer doing it and showing a `toast` with an Undo action. |
| [`context-menu`](#context-menu) | Overlays | Right-click actions on a row, tab, tile or file. It anchors the menu to the wrapped content, not the pointer. For a menu opened by a button use `dropdown`; for the menu rows alone use `menu`. On `tabs`, use its `context` (each tab already sends { tab_menu = id }) and put this around the strip, or a `ui.popover` with `menu`. |
| [`dialog`](#dialog) | Overlays | Any modal that asks for attention: a form, a choice, details. For a yes/no question use `confirm`; for a panel sliding from an edge use `sheet`; for a non-blocking message use `toast` or `notice`; for content beside a control use `ui.popover`. |
| [`emoji-picker`](#emoji-picker) | Overlays | Reacting to a comment or a message, or putting an emoji in a name: open it in a `ui.popover` from an add-reaction button (give the popover `class = "emoji-picker-popover"`). For a list of actions use `menu`; for colours use `swatches`. |
| [`lightbox`](#lightbox) | Overlays | Opening a picture from a document, a gallery or a message to see it large. For a viewer that stays in a pane use `image-viewer`; for a picture at a fixed size use `ui.image`. |
| [`menu`](#menu) | Overlays | The content of any menu: put it in a `ui.popover` or `ui.overlay` yourself, or use `dropdown` (a button that opens one) or `context-menu` (opens on right-click), which already do. For a selectable sidebar list use `list`; for a command palette with a search field use `command-palette`. |
| [`notification-drawer`](#notification-drawer) | Overlays | The app's notification centre, opened from a bell: a list the user filters by kind (All, Error, Success, Info), marks read and dismisses. For transient pop-ups use `toasts`; for a message that stays in the page use `notice`; for any other side panel use `sheet`. |
| [`onboarding`](#onboarding) | Overlays | A short guided tour or welcome on first launch or after a big update. For one release's changes use `release-notes`; for a single question use `confirm`; for any other modal use `dialog`. |
| [`sheet`](#sheet) | Overlays | Side content that needs room but should keep the window in view: details, an inspector, a settings pane, logs. For a centred modal use `dialog`; for a permanent side panel use a `ui.pane` in a split; for a small floating card by a control use `ui.popover`. |
| [`shortcuts`](#shortcuts) | Overlays | Show the app's or a mod's keybindings (a ? or ⌘/ help overlay, a Shortcuts page). For one shortcut use `kbd`; for a line of hints under a list or palette use `key-hints`; for a command palette use `command-palette`. |
| [`status-dot`](#status-dot) | Status | Show the state of an agent, job or session beside its name: in sidebar rows, tabs and lists. Use `chip = true` where the state must catch the eye (a blocked agent). For a count use `count-bubble`; for a PR's state use `pr-badge`; for CI results use `checks`. |
| [`stat`](#stat) | Status bar | One labelled value with an icon in a status bar or toolbar, kept to a fixed width so it does not jitter. |
| [`status-bar`](#status-bar) | Status bar | The window's bottom bar: machine, branch, agent counts on the left; CPU, theme, shortcuts on the right. Put `stat`, `meter` or `sparkline` in it for live readings. For a coloured strip announcing something use `banner`; for a top row use `title-bar`; for an extensible bar, give it a `ui.region` as an item. |
| [`writing-stats`](#writing-stats) | Status bar | Under or beside a writing surface (`prose-editor`), in its status bar, where the writer glances at how far they got. For any other reading in a status bar use `stat`; for progress toward a target use `progress` or `meter`. |
| [`ghostty-terminal`](#ghostty-terminal) | Terminals | A shell drawn by Ghostty's emulator; same as `terminal` with the other engine. |
| [`terminal`](#terminal) | Terminals | A live shell (alacritty engine) filling its space: a pane, a bottom panel. |

### Agents

#### `agent-run`

**Agent Run.** One coding agent's run: status, plan, its latest tool calls, a permission question with the agent's options, and its answer.

**When:** Show what an agent started through `app.acp` is doing or did, with Stop and the answers to its permission questions. For the Send feedback dialog, which lists runs with this, use `feedback`; for a chat transcript use `chat-message`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `lines` | lines of the agent's message shown (default 6; 0 hides it) |
| `request` | show the user's words above |
| `run` | a run from `app.acp.runs` { id, agent, agent_title, text, status, started, finished, error, message, tools, tool_count, plan, question } |
| `to` | where its buttons send, default `provider:acp` |
| `tools` | tool calls listed, newest last (default 4) |

**Styles:** `.agent-run` `.agent-run-accent` `.agent-run-danger` `.agent-run-error` `.agent-run-head` `.agent-run-message` `.agent-run-meta` `.agent-run-muted` `.agent-run-plan` `.agent-run-question` `.agent-run-request` `.agent-run-status` `.agent-run-step` `.agent-run-success` `.agent-run-tool` `.agent-run-tool-title` `.agent-run-warning`

```lua
local agent_run = use "agent-run"

agent_run { request = true, run = { agent = "claude", agent_title = "Claude", id = "1", message = "The status bar is the row at the bottom of app/main.luau; I'll raise its height.", plan = { { content = "Find the status bar's row", status = "completed" }, { content = "Make it 36px tall", status = "in_progress" }, { content = "Run just check", status = "pending" } }, question = { options = { { id = "allow", kind = "allow_once", name = "Allow" }, { id = "always", kind = "allow_always", name = "Always allow" }, { id = "reject", kind = "reject_once", name = "Reject" } }, title = "Edit app/main.luau" }, started = 0, status = "waiting", text = "Make the status bar taller", tool_count = 3, tools = { { id = "a", kind = "read", status = "completed", title = "Read app/main.luau" }, { id = "b", kind = "edit", status = "pending", title = "Edit app/main.luau" } } } }
```

#### `feedback`

**Send Feedback.** A dialog to ask an agent for a change to the app: a text area, a note on who acts on it, Cancel and Send, and the agent runs that came of earlier requests.

**When:** Let the user ask for a change to the app itself, from inside it, and follow what the agent does (`app.acp`). For one run on its own use `agent-run`; for a plain form use `dialog`; for chatting with an agent use `composer`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `actions` | elements on the footer's left, such as an agent `dropdown` |
| `attached` | the element attached to the request, `{ element, at, report }`, shown as a chip; with a `report`, a Copy button beside the chip puts it on the clipboard |
| `change` | sent on each edit, with `value` set to the text |
| `copied` | show "Copied" with a check on the Copy button |
| `copy` | msg the Copy button sends, as well as copying, e.g. to set `copied` |
| `detach` | msg the chip's × sends |
| `dismiss` | msg sent by Cancel, Escape or a backdrop click |
| `error` | why the last send failed, shown above the buttons |
| `expanded` | id of the conversation shown open (its first run), each run with `agent-run`; one waiting on an answer is always open |
| `follow` | show a box to reply in under the open conversation: Reply sends `{ follow = id }` (⌘↩ with `value`), each edit `{ follow_type = id, value }`; start the follow-up with `thread = id` |
| `id` | keeps the text across renders (default "feedback") |
| `inspect` | show an Inspect button that starts Inspect Element for the mod (`command = "inspect"`); the pick comes back on the topic `app/inspect` |
| `note` | muted lines under the field: who acts on the feedback, and what goes with it |
| `open` | show it |
| `placeholder` | grey text while empty (default: two examples) |
| `reply` | the reply the mod has from `follow_type`; Reply is greyed out while it is blank |
| `runs` | runs from `app.acp.runs` the mod started, newest first; runs with a `thread` show under that run as one conversation. A row sends `{ expand = id }`, its × `{ forget_thread = id }` (the mod forgets each run of it) |
| `send` | sent by Send and ⌘↩, with `value` set to the text from ⌘↩ |
| `text` | the text the mod has from `change`; Send is greyed out while it is blank |
| `to` | mod its own messages go to, if not the drawing one |
| `undo` | show Undo these changes under an open conversation whose runs changed the app (`changed`, not yet `undone`): it sends `{ undo_thread = id }`; send the provider `{ undo = run }` for each of its runs, newest first |
| `value` | the text; set it to "" after sending to clear the field |

**Styles:** `.feedback` `.feedback-action` `.feedback-action:hover` `.feedback-attached` `.feedback-body` `.feedback-chip` `.feedback-chip-at` `.feedback-chip-element` `.feedback-detail` `.feedback-done` `.feedback-error` `.feedback-failed` `.feedback-heading` `.feedback-history` `.feedback-item` `.feedback-item-head` `.feedback-item-head:hover` `.feedback-muted` `.feedback-note` `.feedback-reply` `.feedback-request` `.feedback-run` `.feedback-running` `.feedback-said` `.feedback-title` `.feedback-waiting`

```lua
local feedback = use "feedback"

feedback { open = state.open, dismiss = "close", value = state.text, text = state.text,
	change = "type", send = "send", runs = app.acp and app.acp.runs, expanded = state.expanded,
	note = "A background agent changes the app and reports back below." }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/feedback.luau`.

### Containers

#### `accordion`

**Accordion.** Several foldable sections in one frame, one or many open at a time; sends { toggle = id }.

**When:** A stack of foldable sections of the same kind: a merge request's checks, files and activity, or groups of settings. The mod decides whether opening one closes the others. For one foldable block use `collapsible`; for sidebar groups use `sidebar-section`; for switching between views use `tabs`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | key of the msg sent on a header click; default `toggle`, sending `{ toggle = id }` |
| `items` | list of { id, title, summary?, icon?, body (an element or a list of elements) } |
| `open` | the open item's id, or a set `{ [id] = true }` when several may be open |
| `to` | mod to send the msg to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.accordion` `.accordion-divider`

```lua
local accordion = use "accordion"

accordion { open = state.open, items = {
	{ id = "checks", title = "Checks", summary = "3 of 4 passed", icon = "circle-check",
		body = ui.text { "lint, test and build passed; deploy is running.", tone = "muted" } },
	{ id = "files", title = "Files changed", summary = "2", icon = "file",
		body = { ui.text "src/ledger.rs", ui.text "src/currency.rs" } },
} }
-- update: one open at a time: state.open = state.open ~= msg.toggle and msg.toggle or nil
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/accordion.luau`.

#### `card`

**Card.** A rounded, bordered box with a title, an optional subtitle and header actions, and any content.

**When:** A titled box around related content inside a panel or page; for a whole sidebar section use `ui.panel`, for a plain heading use `section`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | the body |
| `actions` | elements on the header's right (buttons, icons) |
| `subtitle` | muted line under the title |
| `title` | heading text |

```lua
local card = use "card"

card { title = "Worktrees", subtitle = "3 checked out",
	actions = { ui.button { "Add", small = true, variant = "ghost", msg = "add" } },
	ui.text "Content goes here.",
}
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/card.luau`.

#### `collapsible`

**Collapsible.** A disclosure header with a chevron, title and summary over a body shown while open.

**When:** One foldable block of content, such as "No agent yet" or advanced options. For several of them stacked use `accordion`; for a titled sidebar group with a count and actions use `sidebar-section`; for a plain heading use `section`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | the body |
| `flat` | no card frame: just the header row and the body |
| `icon` | icon before the title |
| `id` | id for the default toggle msg (default the title) |
| `open` | show the body |
| `summary` | muted text on the header's right (a count, a status) |
| `title` | header text |
| `to` | mod to send the msg to, if not the drawing one |
| `toggle` | msg sent when the header is clicked; default `{ toggle = id }` |

**Styles:** `.collapsible` `.collapsible-body` `.collapsible-chevron` `.collapsible-flat` `.collapsible-header` `.collapsible-header:hover` `.collapsible-header-flat` `.collapsible-summary` `.collapsible-title`

```lua
local collapsible = use "collapsible"
```
