```lua
collapsible { title = "No agent yet", summary = "dispatch one", open = state.agent_open,
	toggle = "toggle-agent",
	ui.text { "Dispatch an agent to work on this merge request in a new worktree.", tone = "muted" },
}
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/collapsible.luau`.

#### `dashboard-card`

**Dashboard Card.** A section of a dashboard: a tinted frame with an uppercase heading, meta and a ⋮ menu, around a white card of content.

**When:** Each block of a dashboard or overview (a chart, a list of things waiting, a table). For a titled box inside a page use `card`; for a sidebar panel use `ui.panel`; for a tiled pane with controls use `pane-frame`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | the content |
| `footer` | elements under the card, on the frame |
| `grow` | fill the parent's free space |
| `icon` | icon before the heading |
| `menu` | message the ⋮ button sends; no button without it |
| `meta` | text or elements on the heading's right (a legend, a count, "Closes Dec 31") |
| `padding` | false: the content touches the card's edges (a table) |
| `title` | the heading, shown in capitals |
| `to` | mod to send `menu` to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.dashboard-card` `.dashboard-card-body` `.dashboard-card-flush` `.dashboard-card-foot` `.dashboard-card-head` `.dashboard-card-meta` `.dashboard-card-title`

```lua
local dashboard_card = use "dashboard-card"

dashboard_card {
	title = "Waiting on you", icon = "inbox", meta = ui.badge "4", menu = "waiting-menu",
	ui.text "…the content…",
}
```

#### `section`

**Section.** A small muted heading over its content, for grouping inside panels.

**When:** A small muted heading over a group of content inside a panel or settings page.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | the content |
| `title` | heading text |

```lua
local section = use "section"

section { title = "Worktrees",
	ui.text "Content goes here.",
}
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/section.luau`.

#### `swap-view`

**Swap View.** Content keyed by a view: when the key changes, the old page fades and folds away as the new one fades and slides in.

**When:** The body under a view switcher (`pill-tabs`, `segmented`, `tabs`) whose content is replaced, such as a list's header and rows per filter. Give `width` so the pages can be measured while they move. For panels that open and close use `side-panels`; for items joining a list give the rows a `key` and a transition instead.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | the page for the current key |
| `grow` | take the free space along the parent's axis |
| `key` | names the page shown: a new key swaps it |
| `width` | the page's width in pixels (default 260); the moving pages keep it, clipped |

**Styles:** `.swap-view-page`

```lua
local swap_view = use "swap-view"

swap_view { key = state.view, width = 260,
	ui.text { TITLES[state.view], weight = "bold" },
	-- ...the rows of that view
}
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/swap-view.luau`.

### Content

#### `browser`

**Browser.** A web page with an address bar: back, forward, reload or stop, an editable address, the title, and open in the system browser.

**When:** A web page in a pane, with browser chrome. Keep the page's `navigate` messages in state and pass the latest as `page`; the address bar navigates on its own. For a bare page without a bar use `ui.browser`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | keeps the page across renders; one per id |
| `loading` | message sent as loads start and finish, with `loading` and `url` added |
| `navigate` | message sent as the page navigates, loads or its title changes; keep it and pass it as `page` |
| `page` | the last `navigate` message: `url`, `title`, `loading`, `back`, `forward` |
| `url` | address to load (http, https, file); a new value navigates |
| `zoom` | page zoom, 0.25 to 5 |

**Styles:** `.browser` `.browser-address` `.browser-bar` `.browser-security` `.browser-title`

```lua
local browser = use "browser"

-- in view: the address bar, history and loading follow `page` by themselves
browser { id = "docs", url = state.url, page = state.page, navigate = { navigated = true } }
-- in update: msg.navigated sets state.page = msg (keep the whole message)
-- to send the page somewhere from code, set state.url to a new address
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/browser.luau`.

#### `chat-markdown`

**Chat Markdown.** Markdown drawn as rich text: bold, italic, code and links in the line, headings, lists, tables, code blocks, quotes, and source chips.

**When:** A chat answer in markdown, including one still streaming in (pass `cursor` while it grows) or citing its sources with `[label](cite:source)` chips. For a whole document, a note or a README use `markdown` (drawn by the host, with links the mod handles); for a file to edit use `markdown-editor`; for plain text use `ui.text`; for a file's source use `code-view`; for ordered steps alone use `numbered-list`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `cursor` | the text is still being written: new words fade in, open marks style what follows them, and a dot follows the last word |
| `link` | message a link click sends, with `url` added, as `markdown` sends it |
| `text` | the markdown; a `[label](cite:source)` link draws a source chip |
| `to` | mod to send `link` to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.chat-markdown`

```lua
local chat_markdown = use "chat-markdown"

chat_markdown { text = "A reply with **bold**, _italic_ and `code` in the line, a [link](https://example.com) and a source chip [Loomwell +1](cite:loomwell).\n\n| Term | Emphasis |\n|---|---|\n| Clay Software | Software that keeps taking the shape of your needs |\n| Live Software | Changes land at once, with no redeploy |\n\n- **Clay Software** — the most memorable.\n- **Self-Rewriting Software** — the most literal.\n\n```lua\nlocal markdown = use \"chat-markdown\"\n```" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/chat-markdown.luau`.

#### `image-viewer`

**Image Viewer.** A picture that fits its space and zooms about the pointer (pinch or ⌘-wheel), pans by wheel or drag, goes between fitted and 100 % on a double-click, with an optional zoom pill and things drawn over the picture.

**When:** Looking at a picture closely: a scan, a photo, a screenshot, a render, with tools drawn over it (a crop frame, picked spots). The mod keeps `zoom` and `center`. For a picture at a fixed size use `ui.image`; for an avatar use `avatar`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `center` | the point of the picture in the middle, { x, y } fractions of it; the middle when unset |
| `change` | message sent as the view changes, with `zoom` (nil when fitted) and `center` added |
| `controls` | a pill in the corner: zoom out, the zoom, zoom in, fit, 100 % |
| `height` | pixels; fills its parent when unset |
| `id` | keeps its state apart from another viewer's in the same mod (default "main") |
| `max` | the most zoom (default 32, 3200 %) |
| `min` | the least zoom (default a quarter of fitted) |
| `overlay` | elements drawn over the picture; their `area` is in fractions of the picture, a `pointer` there takes presses before panning does, and their messages reach the mod as they are |
| `src` | the picture: an absolute or `~/` path (a file the user picked or dropped, the image cache, the app's folders), or one relative to the components folder, which draws it |
| `to` | mod to send view changes to, if not the drawing one |
| `width` | pixels; fills its parent when unset |
| `zoom` | screen pixels per picture pixel (1 is 100 %); nil fits it |

**Styles:** `.image-viewer` `.image-viewer-button` `.image-viewer-button:hover` `.image-viewer-controls` `.image-viewer-zoom`

```lua
local image_viewer = use "image-viewer"

image_viewer { controls = true, height = 280, src = "demos/scan.jpg", width = 420 }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/image-viewer.luau`.

#### `markdown`

**Markdown.** A markdown document: headings, emphasis, lists, task lists, tables, quotes, alerts, footnotes and highlighted code; links send a message instead of opening.

**When:** Show markdown read-only: a README, notes, an agent's answer, release notes written in markdown. For editing a file use `markdown-editor`; for a chat answer streaming in, or one with source chips, use `chat-markdown`; for code alone use `code-view`; for one line of text use `ui.text`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `find` | text to mark wherever it shows |
| `find_index` | which match is current, from 1: marked strongly and scrolled to |
| `found` | message sent as the number of matches changes, with `count` |
| `grow` | fill the parent's free space |
| `image` | message a click on a picture on its own line sends, with `src` and `alt` added, to open it in a `lightbox` |
| `images` | show pictures, from files a `ui.image` could show; never from the web. Without it a picture on its own line shows its alt text |
| `lines` | show at most this many lines, for a preview (not with `scroll`) |
| `link` | message a link click sends, with `url` added (a table gets the field; anything else arrives as { msg = link, url }) |
| `max_width` | pixels: a readable measure for long prose |
| `outline` | message sent as the headings change, with `headings`: { level, text, at, slug }; feed it to `outline` |
| `reveal` | { at = <a heading's `at`>, seq = <a number> }: scrolls there when it changes (with `scroll`); a new `seq` goes there again |
| `scroll` | scroll its own content (with `grow` or a fixed height around it) |
| `section` | message sent as a scrolling document passes a heading, with `heading`, its index |
| `stream` | fade in what is added to `text`, as an answer streams in |
| `text` | the markdown, up to 1 MiB |
| `to` | mod to send its messages to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.markdown`

```lua
local markdown = use "markdown"

markdown { text = state.notes, grow = true, scroll = true, link = "open-link" }
-- update: msg.msg == "open-link" carries the address in msg.url

-- A preview of a note, cut to four lines:
markdown { text = note.body, lines = 4 }

-- A document beside its `outline`, with a `find-bar` over it:
markdown {
	text = state.text, grow = true, scroll = true,
	outline = "headings", section = "reading", reveal = state.reveal,
	find = state.query, find_index = state.match, found = "found",
}
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/markdown.luau`.

#### `markdown-editor`

**Markdown Editor.** A markdown file's source and its rendered preview, side by side or alone, with Save; it never overwrites a file that changed on disk.

**When:** Editing a markdown file of the project in a tab or a pane. For showing markdown without editing use `markdown`; for code read-only use `code-view`; for a short text field use `ui.input`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `id` | keeps the edits apart from another editor's; a tab passes its own |
| `mode` | how it opens: "split" (default), "edit" or "view" |
| `path` | the file, relative to the project's root (as the explorer names it) |
| `root` | the project the file is in, an absolute folder (the explorer's `app.files.path`); the current project when left out |
| `text` | without `path`: a scratch note to start from, edited in place and never saved |

**Styles:** `.md-editor-bar` `.md-editor-dirty` `.md-editor-notice` `.md-editor-path` `.md-editor-source` `.md-editor-status`

```lua
local markdown_editor = use "markdown-editor"

-- In a pane that fills its space; Save needs the drawing mod in
-- providers/docs's `writers` (as shipped, `editor`).
markdown_editor { id = "readme", path = "README.md" }
-- update: msg.open_link is a clicked link's address, msg.from the file it is in, msg.root its project
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/markdown-editor.luau`.

#### `prose-editor`

**Prose Editor.** A distraction-free writing surface: a centred column of text with markdown styled as typed, focus mode that fades all but the current sentence or paragraph, and typewriter scrolling.

**When:** Writing long text: a draft, an article, notes, a journal, where the words are the whole screen. For a markdown file with a preview beside it use `markdown-editor`; for a short field in a form use `ui.input` (with `multiline` for a text area); for a chat box use `composer`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `change` | sent on each edit, with `value` set to the text |
| `dim` | focus mode: "sentence" or "paragraph" stays in full ink, the rest fades; nil shows all |
| `focus` | take keyboard focus when it appears, or when this turns true |
| `id` | keeps the text across renders; give each document its own (default "prose") |
| `keys` | keys the field sends instead of editing while focused: { ['secondary-d'] = "focus" } |
| `markdown` | false writes plain text: no styling of markdown (default true) |
| `measure` | the column's widest width in pixels, a readable line (default 680) |
| `mono` | set the text in the monospace font |
| `placeholder` | grey text while empty (default "Start writing…") |
| `size` | the text's size: normal, large (default) or title |
| `submit` | sent on ⌘↩, with `value` |
| `to` | mod to send its messages to, if not the drawing one |
| `typewriter` | keep the caret's line in the middle of the field |
| `value` | the text; applied when it changes, so opening another document replaces it |

**Styles:** `.prose-editor` `.prose-editor-field` `.prose-editor-field:hover` `.prose-editor-field:focus` `.prose-editor-large` `.prose-editor-normal` `.prose-editor-title`

```lua
local prose_editor = use "prose-editor"

prose_editor { dim = "sentence", measure = 520, value = "# A quiet page\n\nThe sentence being written stays in full ink. The rest of the page steps back, so the next word is all there is.\n\nMarkdown takes its shape as it is typed: *emphasis*, **strong**, `code`." }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/prose-editor.luau`.

#### `video-viewer`

**Video Viewer.** Live frames from another process that fit their space and zoom, pan by wheel or drag, go between fitted and 100 % on a double-click, and read the pixel under a press, with the controls under the picture.

**When:** Previewing a camera or scanner, or inspecting a full-resolution frame, with an engine writing a frame ring (`ui.video`). The mod keeps `zoom` and `center`. For a picture in a file use `image-viewer`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `black` | the code value shown as black |
| `center` | the point of the picture in the middle, { x, y } fractions of it |
| `change` | message sent as the view changes, with `zoom` (nil when fitted), `center` and `viewed = true` added |
| `color` | what the pixels are: srgb, display-p3, rec709, rec2020, linear-srgb, linear-p3, or none to send them to the screen as they are |
| `controls` | a row under the picture: zoom out, the zoom, zoom in, fit, 100 % |
| `extended` | lets values above 1 reach a screen that can show them |
| `gain` | multiplies the result |
| `gamma` | a display gamma to encode with; 1 changes nothing |
| `guides` | rectangles and lines the host draws in the picture: { x, y, width, height, color } in fractions of it |
| `height` | pixels; fills its parent when unset |
| `id` | keeps its state apart from another viewer's in the same mod (default "main") |
| `max` | the most zoom (default 32) |
| `probed` | message sent with `x`, `y`, `source`, `display` and on a Bayer frame `channel` added, for the pixel pressed |
| `source` | the frame ring's name, as the engine made it |
| `stats` | message sent each second with `fps`, `shown`, `skipped`, `latency` (ms), `live`, `width`, `height`, `format`, `frame`, `fit` and `density` added |
| `white` | the code value shown as white (4095 for 12 bits in 16); the format's full range when unset |
| `width` | pixels; fills its parent when unset |
| `zoom` | device pixels per picture pixel (1 is 100 %); nil fits it |

**Styles:** `.video-viewer` `.video-viewer-button` `.video-viewer-button:hover` `.video-viewer-controls` `.video-viewer-zoom`

```lua
local video_viewer = use "video-viewer"

video_viewer { controls = true, height = 280, source = "preview", width = 420 }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/video-viewer.luau`.

### Controls

#### `button-group`

**Button Group.** Buttons joined into one bordered group with dividers, text or icons, optionally one selected; sends { select = id }.

**When:** Related actions or view modes side by side in a header: Unified | Split, Uncommitted | Branch, zoom − | +. For a settings choice in a track use `segmented`; for separate quiet buttons use `toolbar`; for back/forward use `nav-buttons`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `buttons` | list of { id, label?, icon?, tooltip?, selected?, disabled?, msg? (sent instead of the default) } |
| `event` | key of the message a click sends, default "select": { select = id } |
| `selected` | id of the selected button (or mark buttons `selected`) |
| `small` | smaller buttons |
| `to` | mod to send messages to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.button-group` `.button-group-button` `.button-group-button:hover` `.button-group-button:selected` `.button-group-disabled` `.button-group-separator` `.button-group-small`

```lua
local button_group = use "button-group"

button_group { buttons = { { icon = "rows-2", id = "unified", label = "Unified" }, { icon = "columns-2", id = "split", label = "Split" }, { icon = "refresh-cw", id = "refresh", msg = "refresh", tooltip = "Refresh" } }, selected = "unified" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/button-group.luau`.

#### `caffeine`

**Caffeine.** A cup that keeps the machine awake while on, so a long job is not cut off by sleep.

**When:** A scan, render or copy that runs unattended: put it in a status bar or toolbar for the user to turn on. A mod that knows when its job starts and ends should send `app:awake` itself instead.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `awake` | `app.awake`, for it to show how things stand |
| `disabled` | greys it out: for while a job holds by itself, which the cup can't let go of |
| `reason` | why, for the system's list of what is keeping it awake |
| `scope` | "display" keeps the screen on too (default); "system" lets it sleep and lock |
| `size` | as `icon-button` |
| `variant` | as `icon-button` |

```lua
local caffeine = use "caffeine"

caffeine { awake = app.awake, scope = "system", reason = "Scanning" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/caffeine.luau`.

#### `chips`

**Chips.** Filter pills that toggle on and off, with an optional icon and count; a click sends { toggle = id }.

**When:** Filters over a list where any number can be on (Open, Mine, Has agent). For exactly one of a few use `segmented`; for read-only labels use `tags`; for a single on/off setting use `switch`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `chips` | list of { id, label, icon?, count?, on? (or list ids in `selected`), msg? (sent instead of the default) } |
| `event` | key of the message a click sends, default "toggle": { toggle = id } |
| `selected` | ids of the chips that are on (instead of each chip's `on`) |
| `to` | mod to send messages to, if not the drawing one |
| `wrap` | wrap onto more lines when narrow (default true) |

**Styles:** `.chips` `.chips-chip` `.chips-chip:hover` `.chips-chip:selected` `.chips-count` `.chips-count:selected`

```lua
local chips = use "chips"

chips { chips = { { count = 12, id = "open", label = "Open" }, { count = 3, icon = "user", id = "mine", label = "Mine" }, { count = 5, icon = "agent-claude", id = "agent", label = "Has agent" }, { icon = "git-pull-request-draft", id = "draft", label = "Draft" }, { count = 1, icon = "circle-x", id = "failing", label = "CI failing" } }, selected = { "open", "agent" } }
```

**Copy Field.** Monospace text in a bordered box with a Copy button that puts it on the clipboard, and a "Copied" state.

| `button` | button text (default "Copy") |
| `copied` | show "Copied" with a check in the success colour (the mod sets it after `msg`, then clears it) |
| `label` | small muted heading above the box |
| `msg` | message sent on the click as well, e.g. to set `copied` |
| `text` | the text shown and copied |
| `to` | mod to send `msg` to, if not the drawing one |

#### `dropdown`

**Dropdown.** A button with the current value and a chevron that opens a menu of options under it; picking sends { pick = id }.

**When:** Pick one of many options that do not fit a `segmented` control (more than 3 or 4, or long labels), or a button that opens a menu of actions. For 2 to 4 short choices use `segmented`; for a menu on right-click use `context-menu`; for the menu rows alone use `menu`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `align` | "start" (default) or "end": which edge of the button the menu lines up with |
| `chevron` | icon at the button's end (default "chevron-down"; "chevrons-up-down" for a select) |
| `disabled` | greys the button out and ignores clicks |
| `dismiss` | message sent on a click outside or Escape |
| `event` | key of the message a pick sends, default "pick": { pick = id } |
| `expand` | key of the message an item with a submenu sends, default "expand": { expand = id } |
| `expanded` | id of the item whose submenu shows (an item with `items`), passed to `menu` |
| `highlighted` | keyboard-highlighted option (id or index), passed to `menu` |
| `icon` | icon before the text |
| `keys` | more keys while open, e.g. { up = "prev", down = "next", enter = "choose" }; escape sends `dismiss` |
| `label` | muted text before the value ("Shell") |
| `open` | true while the menu shows |
| `options` | `menu` items: { id, label, icon?, shortcut?, detail?, danger?, disabled? }, "separator", { heading = ... } |
| `placeholder` | button text when nothing is selected |
| `selected` | id of the current option; it gets a check |
| `side` | "bottom" (default) or "top" |
| `submenu_highlighted` | keyboard-highlighted row of the open submenu (id or index) |
| `to` | mod to send messages to, if not the drawing one |
| `toggle` | message the button sends (open or close) |
| `trigger_width` | the button's width in pixels, the chevron pushed to its end (default: as wide as its text) |
| `value` | text on the button; defaults to the selected option's label |
| `width` | menu width in pixels (default 220) |

**Styles:** `.dropdown-chevron` `.dropdown-disabled` `.dropdown-icon` `.dropdown-label` `.dropdown-popover` `.dropdown-trigger` `.dropdown-trigger:hover` `.dropdown-trigger:selected`

```lua
local dropdown = use "dropdown"

dropdown {
	label = "Shell", icon = "terminal",
	open = state.shell_open, toggle = "toggle-shell", dismiss = "close-shell",
	selected = state.shell,
	options = {
		{ id = "zsh", label = "zsh", detail = "/bin/zsh" },
		{ id = "fish", label = "fish" },
		"separator",
		{ id = "custom", label = "Custom…", icon = "settings" },
	},
}
-- update: msg == "toggle-shell" flips state.shell_open; msg.pick sets
-- state.shell and closes it; "close-shell" closes it.
```

#### `filter-dropdown`

**Filter Dropdown.** A filter chip with an icon, its value ("Any author") and a chevron that opens a menu; one or several options, an accent look when on, and an optional × to clear.

**When:** Filters in a row over a table or list (activity type, author, date range), each narrowing it to one or a few values. For toggles that are each on or off use `chips`; for a setting rather than a filter use `dropdown`; for a free-text filter use `search-field`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `any` | label of an option at the top that clears the filter (sends { [event] = "" }); none when unset |
| `clear` | message for an × on the chip while a filter is on; no × when unset |
| `dismiss` | message sent on a click outside or Escape |
| `event` | key of the message a pick sends, default "pick": { pick = id } |
| `icon` | icon before the value |
| `label` | muted text before the value ("Author") |
| `multiple` | several options can be on; a pick toggles one and the menu stays open |
| `open` | true while the menu shows |
| `options` | `menu` items: { id, label, icon?, detail? }, "separator", { heading = ... } |
| `placeholder` | text while nothing is picked ("Any author") |
| `plain` | keep the resting look when a filter is on (no accent) |
| `selected` | the picked id, or with `multiple` a list of ids |
| `to` | mod to send messages to, if not the drawing one |
| `toggle` | message the chip sends (open or close) |
| `width` | menu width in pixels (default 220) |

**Styles:** `.filter-dropdown` `.filter-dropdown:hover` `.filter-dropdown:selected` `.filter-dropdown-chevron` `.filter-dropdown-clear` `.filter-dropdown-clear:hover` `.filter-dropdown-icon` `.filter-dropdown-label` `.filter-dropdown-on` `.filter-dropdown-on:hover` `.filter-dropdown-popover`

```lua
local filter_dropdown = use "filter-dropdown"

filter_dropdown {
	icon = "user", placeholder = "Any author", any = "Any author",
	open = state.open == "author", toggle = { open = "author" }, dismiss = "close",
	event = "author", selected = state.author,
	options = { { id = "nadia", label = "Nadia Okafor" }, { id = "theo", label = "Theo Lind" } },
}
-- update: msg.author sets state.author ("" clears it) and closes the menu.
-- With multiple = true, selected is a list and each pick toggles one id.
```

#### `icon-button`

**Icon Button.** A square icon-only button with a tooltip: ghost, outline or solid, small or normal, optionally pressed or with a count.

**When:** An action or toggle shown only as an icon: in a title bar, a panel header, a toolbar. Always give a `tooltip`. For buttons with words use `ui.button` or `toolbar`; for back/forward use `nav-buttons`; for joined icon choices use `button-group`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `active` | show it pressed, for a toggle that is on |
| `badge` | a small count or dot text beside the icon |
| `command` | an app command to run instead of `msg` |
| `disabled` | greys it out and ignores clicks |
| `icon` | icon name |
| `msg` | message a click sends |
| `size` | "normal" (32px, default) or "small" (26px) |
| `to` | mod to send `msg` to, if not the drawing one |
| `tone` | "danger" for a destructive action |
| `tooltip` | text shown under the pointer (also its name for the user) |
| `variant` | "ghost" (default), "outline" or "solid" |

**Styles:** `.icon-button` `.icon-button:hover` `.icon-button:selected` `.icon-button-badge` `.icon-button-danger` `.icon-button-danger:hover` `.icon-button-disabled` `.icon-button-outline` `.icon-button-outline:selected` `.icon-button-small` `.icon-button-solid` `.icon-button-solid:hover` `.icon-button-solid:selected`

```lua
local icon_button = use "icon-button"

icon_button { icon = "panel-left", tooltip = "Toggle sidebar", msg = "sidebar", active = state.sidebar }
icon_button { icon = "bell", tooltip = "Notifications", msg = "notifications", variant = "outline", badge = 3 }
icon_button { icon = "delete", tooltip = "Delete", msg = "delete", size = "small", tone = "danger" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/icon-button.luau`.

#### `picker`

**Picker.** A field's value as a quiet pill that opens a searchable list of options (people, labels, statuses); one or several, with a Create row; picking sends { pick = id }.

**When:** A property of a record set from many options: assignee, labels, project, status, priority, "blocked by", in a task's detail panel or a row. For a setting in a form use `dropdown`; for a filter over a list use `filter-dropdown`; for 2 to 4 short choices use `segmented`; for addresses use `recipient-field`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `align` | "start" (default) or "end": which edge of the trigger the popover lines up with |
| `create` | message of a "Create “text”" row under the list, shown while the query matches no label exactly; sent with `value` set to the query |
| `dismiss` | message sent on a click outside or Escape |
| `empty` | text while no option matches the query (default "No matches") |
| `event` | key of the message a pick sends, default "pick": { pick = id } |
| `highlight` | key of the message up and down send, default "highlight": { highlight = id } of the next row; Enter picks the highlighted row (or sends `create`) |
| `highlighted` | id of the keyboard-highlighted option ("+create" for the Create row); the first shown one when unset or filtered out |
| `icon` | icon before the placeholder, and before a picked option that has no icon, avatar or dot of its own |
| `id` | keeps the search text across renders (default "picker") |
| `keys` | more keys while open, e.g. { tab = "next-field" }; they replace the built-in up, down and enter |
| `multiple` | several can be picked: each pick toggles one (the mod keeps the popover open) and the trigger shows them all (pills, avatars, or the first label and how many more) |
| `open` | true while the popover shows |
| `options` | list of { id, label, detail? (muted, on the right), icon?, avatar? (a person's name: a small round `avatar`), dot? (a colour: a small dot, as for a status), color? (a coloured label: a dot in the list, a `pill` on the trigger), disabled? } |
| `placeholder` | trigger text while nothing is picked ("Add labels"), muted after `icon` |
| `query` | the search text; the list shows the options whose label holds it, case aside (set it to "" on close) |
| `search` | message sent on each edit of the search field, with `value` set to the text; no search field when unset |
| `selected` | the picked id, or with `multiple` a list of ids |
| `to` | mod to send messages to, if not the drawing one |
| `toggle` | message the trigger sends (open or close) |
| `trigger` | an element to open it from instead of the pill (it sends `toggle` itself) |
| `width` | popover width in pixels (default 240) |

**Styles:** `.picker-dot` `.picker-empty` `.picker-faces` `.picker-icon` `.picker-pills` `.picker-placeholder` `.picker-popover` `.picker-search` `.picker-search-icon` `.picker-search-input` `.picker-trigger` `.picker-trigger:hover` `.picker-trigger:selected`

```lua
local picker = use "picker"

picker {
	options = PEOPLE, selected = task.assignee, icon = "user", placeholder = "Assign",
	open = state.open == "assignee", toggle = { open = "assignee" }, dismiss = "close",
	query = state.query, search = "search", highlighted = state.highlighted,
}
-- update: msg.open opens (or closes) it; "close" closes it and sets
-- state.query = ""; msg.msg == "search" sets state.query = msg.value;
-- msg.highlight sets state.highlighted; msg.pick sets task.assignee and
-- closes it. With multiple = true, selected is a list and each pick
-- toggles one id; with create = "create", msg.value is the new label.
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/picker.luau`.

#### `segmented`

**Segmented.** One-of-many choice as segments in a rounded track, the selected one raised; sends { select = id }.

**When:** A setting with 2 to 4 short, mutually exclusive values (Light / Dark / System, All / Mine). For more or longer options use `dropdown`; for a vertical list with descriptions use `radio-group`; for switching documents or views use `tabs`; for actions rather than a choice use `button-group`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | key of the message a click sends, default "select": { select = id } |
| `grow` | fill the width, segments sharing it equally |
| `options` | list of { id, label?, icon? (optional, before the label), count? (a number or text after the label, in the accent colour), tooltip?, msg? (sent instead of the default) }; an icon without a label makes an icon-only segment |
| `selected` | id of the chosen option |
| `small` | tighter segments, for a dense toolbar |
| `to` | mod to send messages to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.segmented` `.segmented-count` `.segmented-option` `.segmented-option:hover` `.segmented-option:selected` `.segmented-small`

```lua
local segmented = use "segmented"

segmented { options = { { id = "light", label = "Light" }, { id = "dark", label = "Dark" }, { id = "system", label = "System" } }, selected = "dark" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/segmented.luau`.

#### `toolbar`

**Toolbar.** Small ghost buttons in a row; each sends its msg to the mod drawing it, or runs a command.

**When:** A row of small quiet buttons above a panel or list. For icon-only buttons use `icon-button`; for one-of-many choices use `segmented`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `buttons` | list of { label, msg or command, variant } |

```lua
local toolbar = use "toolbar"

toolbar { buttons = { { label = "New", msg = "new" }, { label = "Refresh", msg = "refresh" }, { label = "Remove", msg = "remove", variant = "danger" } } }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/toolbar.luau`.

### Data

#### `audio-meter`

**Audio Meter.** A vertical bar per channel in dBFS, with a held peak and colours near full scale.

**When:** Sound levels while recording or playing, from values an engine published. For a fraction that isn't sound use `vertical-bar` or `meter`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `bar` | each bar's width in pixels (default 10) |
| `channels` | list of { level, peak?, name? }, levels in dBFS (0 is full scale) |
| `danger` | the level it turns to the danger colour at (default -3) |
| `floor` | the level at the bottom, in dBFS (default -60) |
| `height` | pixels (default 140) |
| `warn` | the level it turns to the warning colour at (default -12) |

**Styles:** `.audio-meter-danger` `.audio-meter-fill` `.audio-meter-label` `.audio-meter-peak` `.audio-meter-track` `.audio-meter-warn`

```lua
local audio_meter = use "audio-meter"

audio_meter { channels = { { level = -18, name = "L", peak = -9 }, { level = -14, name = "R", peak = -2 } }, height = 120 }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/audio-meter.luau`.

#### `avatar`

**Avatar.** A name's initial on a colour picked from the name (six-colour palette), square or round, with an optional status dot on its corner.

**When:** Stand for a person, space, project or agent by its name: comment authors, workspace switchers, people lists. Use `comment-card` for an authored message (it draws one), `status-dot` for a state alone.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `color` | a colour instead of the one picked from the name |
| `initial` | letters to show instead of the name's first letter |
| `letters` | how many initials to take from the name's words: 1 (default) or 2 ("Alex Kim" shows AK) |
| `name` | the name the initial and colour come from |
| `shape` | square (rounded, default) \| circle |
| `size` | small \| normal \| large \| xlarge (18, 24, 32, 44 px) |
| `src` | an image file (relative to the mod's folder, `~/...` or absolute; not a URL: a provider downloads it to ~/.cache/moonframe/images) shown instead of the initial; a missing file leaves the coloured tile |
| `status` | working \| blocked \| done \| idle \| unknown: a status dot on the corner |
| `tooltip` | text under the pointer (default the name) |

**Styles:** `.avatar` `.avatar-circle` `.avatar-image` `.avatar-image-circle` `.avatar-status` `.avatar-status-blocked` `.avatar-status-done` `.avatar-status-idle` `.avatar-status-unknown` `.avatar-status-working`

```lua
local avatar = use "avatar"

avatar { name = "harbor-docs", size = "xlarge", status = "working" }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/avatar.luau`.

#### `avatar-stack`

**Avatar Stack.** Up to a few overlapping round avatars, then the group's size.

**When:** Who is in a group, in a card or a row (38 investors, 3 reviewers), when their names matter less than how many. For one person use `avatar`; for a list of people use `list` or `table`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `count` | the group's size, shown after them (default the number of people) |
| `most` | the most avatars drawn (default 3) |
| `people` | list of { name, src? }: the avatars drawn |
| `size` | avatar size: small (default) or normal |

**Styles:** `.avatar-stack` `.avatar-stack-count` `.avatar-stack-face` `.avatar-stack-faces`

```lua
local avatar_stack = use "avatar-stack"

avatar_stack { count = 38, people = { { name = "Cole Bennett" }, { name = "Imani Bennett" }, { name = "Ray Ortiz" }, { name = "Mia Chen" } } }
```

#### `bar-chart`

**Bar Chart.** Vertical bars per bucket, stacked by series with toned colours, axis labels, an optional scale, and a legend.

**When:** Counts over time or per category: tokens per day, runs per hour, alerts per device, stacked by kind. For a tiny live trend in a status bar use `sparkline`; for one fraction use `meter`; for one headline number use `stat-tile`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `axis` | show the top value and 0 on the left |
| `bar` | bar width in pixels (default 18) |
| `buckets` | list of { label, values = { one number per series }, tooltip, dim (drawn faded: a period still running) } |
| `every` | label every Nth bucket (default 1) |
| `gap` | pixels between bucket slots (default 4) |
| `grid` | false hides the gridlines `ticks` draws |
| `grow` | the buckets share the width given instead of taking `slot` pixels each |
| `height` | plot height in pixels (default 120) |
| `legend` | false hides the legend |
| `max` | value at the top (default the largest stack) |
| `series` | list of { name, tone (accent\|success\|warning\|danger\|muted\|c1..c6), color (hex) }; bottom of the stack first |
| `slot` | pixels each bucket takes, bar plus room for its label (default 30) |
| `ticks` | steps on the scale: labels from 0 to `max` at each step, with dashed gridlines (implies `axis`) |
| `unit` | suffix for the scale, e.g. "k" or "%" |

**Styles:** `.bar-chart` `.bar-chart-accent` `.bar-chart-bar` `.bar-chart-c1` `.bar-chart-c2` `.bar-chart-c3` `.bar-chart-c4` `.bar-chart-c5` `.bar-chart-c6` `.bar-chart-danger` `.bar-chart-dim` `.bar-chart-empty` `.bar-chart-grid` `.bar-chart-key` `.bar-chart-label` `.bar-chart-legend` `.bar-chart-muted` `.bar-chart-plot` `.bar-chart-scale` `.bar-chart-success` `.bar-chart-swatch` `.bar-chart-warning`

```lua
local bar_chart = use "bar-chart"

bar_chart {
	axis = true, unit = "k", height = 120,
	series = { { name = "Input", tone = "c1" }, { name = "Output", tone = "c4" }, { name = "Cache", tone = "muted" } },
	buckets = {
		{ label = "Mon", values = { 42, 18, 12 } },
		{ label = "Tue", values = { 55, 22, 20 } },
		-- ...
	},
}
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/bar-chart.luau`.

#### `chat-message`

**Chat Message.** A chat message: the user's as a bubble on the right, the assistant's as text under an icon and a name, with anything else inside.

**When:** Each turn of a conversation with an agent or a person, stacked in a scrolling column over a `composer`. For a comment on a pull request use `comment-card`; for a notification use `toast`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | more after the text: a `thinking` fold, cards, lists |
| `author` | the assistant's name in its header; no header without it |
| `from` | "user" (a bubble on the right) or "assistant" (default) |
| `icon` | the icon in the header's chip (default sparkles) |
| `text` | the message's text; paragraphs split on blank lines |

**Styles:** `.chat-message` `.chat-message-author` `.chat-message-bubble` `.chat-message-chip` `.chat-message-head`

```lua
local chat_message = use "chat-message"
local thinking = use "thinking"

chat_message { from = "user", text = "Which deal should I look at first?" }
chat_message {
	author = "Sales agent", text = "Start with Lumen Retail: the biggest deal at risk.",
	thinking { seconds = 4, open = state.thought, msg = "toggle-thought" },
}
```

#### `code-view`

**Code View.** Read-only mono lines, colored by language, with line numbers, highlighted lines, a start line and an optional path header; no wrapping; scrolls.

**When:** Show code or a log read-only: a file at a line, a snippet in a comment, a test's output. For changes use `diff-view`; for a live shell use `terminal`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | line click message key: sends { [event] = line number } (no click without it) |
| `grow` | fill the parent and scroll |
| `height` | pixels: scrolls within it |
| `highlight` | line numbers to highlight |
| `id` | names the list a long scrolling view becomes (default "code-view"); two long views in one mod need two |
| `language` | color the code as this language ("rust", "lua"); the extension of `path` when unset. A line at a time, so a block comment over several lines colors only where it shows it |
| `lines` | the lines instead of `text` |
| `numbers` | false hides line numbers |
| `path` | a header with the file path |
| `start` | number of the first line (default 1) |
| `text` | the code; split into lines on \n |
| `to` | the mod to send it to |

**Styles:** `.code-view` `.code-view-body` `.code-view-gutter` `.code-view-header` `.code-view-header-icon` `.code-view-highlight` `.code-view-line` `.code-view-line:hover` `.code-view-number` `.code-view-path` `.code-view-text`

```lua
local code_view = use "code-view"

code_view {
	path = "src/ledger.rs", start = 24, highlight = { 26, 27 }, height = 230,
	text = state.source, -- or lines = { "impl Book {", ... }
}
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/code-view.luau`.

#### `comment-card`

**Comment Card.** An authored message: avatar, bold author, "commented 3d ago", an optional file:line chip, a role badge, the body, and reactions with a button to add one.

**When:** Comments in a pull request conversation, review threads, notes left by agents or people. Stack them in a column. For a numbered review note with a remove button use `note-card`; for events in order use `timeline`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | anything after the body: a code-view, a diff-view, buttons |
| `action` | verb after the name (default "commented"), e.g. "approved", "requested changes" |
| `actions` | elements at the header's right |
| `add_reaction` | message the add-reaction button sends; no button without it. With `picker`, a click outside the open picker or Escape sends it again, so the mod toggles |
| `age` | age text, e.g. "3d ago" |
| `author` | author name (the avatar's initial and colour come from it) |
| `avatar` | an image file for the avatar |
| `badge` | a small role tag after the name: "author", "bot" |
| `body` | the text; blank lines split paragraphs |
| `locate` | message the chip sends on a click (e.g. { open = "src/ledger.rs:26" }) |
| `location` | a file:line chip, e.g. "src/ledger.rs:26" |
| `picker` | an element, usually `emoji-picker`, shown in a popover on the add-reaction button |
| `picker_open` | show `picker` |
| `react` | the key a reaction's click sends its emoji under (default "react": `{ react = "👍" }`) |
| `reactions` | list of { emoji, count, mine?, tooltip? }: pills under the body, `mine` tinted (the reader's own) |
| `seconds` | age in seconds instead of `age` |
| `to` | the mod to send `locate` to |

**Styles:** `.comment-card` `.comment-card-add-reaction` `.comment-card-add-reaction:hover` `.comment-card-add-reaction:selected` `.comment-card-author` `.comment-card-badge` `.comment-card-badge-text` `.comment-card-body` `.comment-card-location` `.comment-card-location:hover` `.comment-card-location-text` `.comment-card-meta` `.comment-card-reaction` `.comment-card-reaction:hover` `.comment-card-reaction-count` `.comment-card-reaction-emoji` `.comment-card-reaction-mine` `.comment-card-reaction-mine:hover` `.comment-card-reactions` `.comment-card-text`

```lua
local comment_card = use "comment-card"

comment_card { action = "requested changes", add_reaction = "add-reaction", age = "3d ago", author = "alice", badge = "reviewer", body = "Reject mixing currencies here: return a Result instead of silently grouping.\n\nA builder would also keep the call sites short.", location = "src/ledger.rs:26", reactions = { { count = 3, emoji = "👍", mine = true }, { count = 1, emoji = "🎉", mine = false } } }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/comment-card.luau`.

#### `contribution-graph`

**Contribution Graph.** A year of days as squares in week columns, shaded by count, with months on top, weekdays on the side, a tooltip per day and a Less … More legend.

**When:** Daily activity over months or a year, GitHub style: commits, agent runs, posts, workouts, a streak. Pass one count per day and the first day's date. For weekly or arbitrary buckets without dates use `heat-grid`; for counts with an axis use `bar-chart`; for picking a day use `month-grid`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `color` | the busiest colour, lighter levels tinted from it (default success) |
| `days` | one count per day, oldest first |
| `empty` | a day with nothing (default muted-foreground at 12%) |
| `event` | key of the message a day sends: { [event] = "YYYY-MM-DD" }; days are not clickable without it |
| `gap` | pixels between squares (default 3) |
| `legend` | false hides the Less … More legend |
| `months` | false hides the month labels |
| `note` | muted text on the legend's left, e.g. "Learn how we count contributions" |
| `note_msg` | message a click on the note sends |
| `noun` | what is counted (default "contribution") |
| `nouns` | its plural (default the noun with an s) |
| `palette` | colours from empty to busiest, e.g. GitHub's { "#161b22", "#0e4429", "#006d32", "#26a641", "#39d353" }; one more than the thresholds |
| `selected` | the chosen day, "YYYY-MM-DD", outlined |
| `size` | a square's side in pixels (default 11) |
| `start` | the first day's date, "YYYY-MM-DD" |
| `thresholds` | the smallest count of each level, e.g. { 1, 3, 6, 10 }; default quarters of the busiest day |
| `to` | mod to send it to, if not the drawing one |
| `week_start` | "sunday" (default) or "monday": the top row |
| `weekdays` | false hides the Mon / Wed / Fri labels |

**Styles:** `.contribution-graph` `.contribution-graph-cell` `.contribution-graph-cell:hover` `.contribution-graph-cell:selected` `.contribution-graph-legend` `.contribution-graph-month` `.contribution-graph-note` `.contribution-graph-note:hover` `.contribution-graph-weekday`

```lua
local contribution_graph = use "contribution-graph"

contribution_graph {
	start = "2025-11-02",       -- the first count's date
	days = state.counts,        -- one count per day, oldest first
	note = "Learn how we count contributions", note_msg = "help",
	event = "day", selected = state.day,   -- a click sends { day = "2026-05-14" }
	-- palette = { "#161b22", "#0e4429", "#006d32", "#26a641", "#39d353" },
}
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/contribution-graph.luau`.

| `count` | the number |

| `max` | largest number shown before "N+" (default 99) |

| `tooltip` | text under the pointer |
| `zero` | show 0 instead of nothing |

**Styles:** `.count-bubble` `.count-bubble-danger` `.count-bubble-muted` `.count-bubble-success` `.count-bubble-text` `.count-bubble-warning`

#### `course-card`

**Course Card.** A featured course or program: eyebrow, title, facts, a Continue button and a second action, a progress line, and a slot on the right.

**When:** The one course, plan or program a page puts first, with where the reader is and a button to carry on. For a grid of guides use `guide-card`; for a figure with a trend use `stat-tile`; for a titled box of anything use `card`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `aside` | an element on the right, such as a `heat-grid` |
| `bar` | the bar's width in pixels (default 240) |
| `detail` | text over the bar's right (default the percentage) |

| `primary` | { label, icon?, msg }: the dark button (Continue lesson 4) |
| `progress` | 0 to 1: the bar |
| `secondary` | { label, icon?, msg }: the outlined button beside it |
| `title` | the course's name |
| `to` | mod to send the buttons' msgs to, if not the drawing one |

```lua
	meta = "8 lessons · 46 min · Beginner",
	primary = { label = "Continue lesson 4", icon = "play", msg = "continue" },
	secondary = { label = "View syllabus", icon = "book-open", msg = "syllabus" },
	progress = 3 / 8, label = "3 of 8 lessons",
```

#### `date-tile`

**Date Tile.** A small calendar leaf: the month on a coloured band over the day's number.

**When:** Beside dated items in a list (deadlines, calls, distributions, events) where the date leads. For a date inside a line of text use plain text; for picking a day use `day-strip` or `month-grid`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `day` | the day's number |
| `month` | the month, short ("Nov"); shown in capitals |
| `size` | "normal" (default, 48 px) or "small" (38 px) |
| `tone` | the band: neutral (default, dark), danger or accent |

**Styles:** `.date-tile` `.date-tile-accent` `.date-tile-band` `.date-tile-danger` `.date-tile-day` `.date-tile-month`

```lua
local date_tile = use "date-tile"

date_tile { day = "9", month = "Nov", tone = "danger" }
```

#### `document-card`

**Document Card.** A document as a grid tile: its title, a preview of its first lines rendered as markdown, the date it changed and a star.

**When:** A home screen or a folder of notes shown as a grid. For a list beside an editor use `document-row`; for attached files use `file-card`; for reading material with progress use `guide-card`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `context` | message a right-click sends (a menu) |
| `date` | when it last changed, as shown ("Today, 14:02") |
| `favorite` | draw the star filled |
| `height` | pixels (default 200) |
| `lines` | lines of preview shown (default 5) |
| `msg` | message a click sends (open it) |
| `selected` | highlight it |
| `star` | message the star sends; no star without it |
| `text` | its markdown, cut to `lines` lines |
| `title` | the document's title |
| `to` | mod to send them to, if not the drawing one |
| `width` | pixels (default 240) |

**Styles:** `.document-card` `.document-card:hover` `.document-card:selected` `.document-card-date` `.document-card-preview` `.document-card-title`

```lua
local document_card = use "document-card"

ui.row { wrap = true, gap = "large",
	document_card { title = note.title, text = note.body, date = note.changed,
		favorite = note.starred, star = { star = note.id }, msg = { open = note.id } },
}
```

#### `dot-chart`

**Dot Chart.** Columns of rounded squares, one per bucket: filled for this period, pale up to the previous period's value; with an axis and labels.

**When:** A daily or weekly count compared with the period before (signups, orders), where the squares' rhythm reads better than smooth bars. For stacked counts by kind use `bar-chart`; for a balance against a floor use `forecast-chart`; for a trend line use `ui.line`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `color` | this period's colour (default accent) |
| `columns` | list of { current, previous?, tooltip? }, left to right |
| `labels` | labels under the chart, spread evenly from the first column to the last |
| `max` | the value at the top |
| `rows` | squares in a full column (default 8): each is max / rows |
| `shade` | the previous period's colour (default muted-foreground at 12%) |
| `size` | a square's side in pixels (default 13) |
| `ticks` | axis labels from the top (max) down to 0, evenly spaced |

**Styles:** `.dot-chart` `.dot-chart-column` `.dot-chart-dot` `.dot-chart-label` `.dot-chart-tick`

```lua
local dot_chart = use "dot-chart"

dot_chart { columns = { { current = 48, previous = 60 }, { current = 70, previous = 61 }, { current = 55, previous = 66 }, { current = 90, previous = 85 }, { current = 82, previous = 74 }, { current = 104, previous = 118 } }, labels = { "Oct 2", "Oct 5", "Oct 8" }, max = 120, rows = 8, ticks = { "120", "60", "0" } }
```

#### `file-card`

**File Card.** An attached file: a thumbnail or its type's icon, the name, a muted line, a remove button, and a bar while it uploads; as a tile or a row.

**When:** Attachments on a task, a comment or a message, in a grid of tiles or a list of rows, while they upload and after. For the area files are dropped on use `dropzone`; for a file in a tree use `tree` with `file-icon`; for a picture to look at closely use `image-viewer`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `detail` | a muted line under the name, e.g. "PDF · 2.4 MB" |
| `layout` | "tile" (default: thumbnail on top, for a grid) or "row" (icon at the left, for a list) |
| `msg` | message a click sends (open or preview it) |
| `name` | the file's name; its extension picks the icon when there is no thumbnail |
| `progress` | 0 to 1 while it uploads: a bar and the percentage instead of `detail` |
| `remove` | message the × sends; no × without it |
| `selected` | highlight it |
| `src` | a picture file for the thumbnail (cropped to fill) |
| `to` | mod to send the messages to, if not the drawing one |
| `width` | pixels (default 168 for a tile; a row grows) |

**Styles:** `.file-card` `.file-card:hover` `.file-card:selected` `.file-card-body` `.file-card-detail` `.file-card-fill` `.file-card-icon` `.file-card-name` `.file-card-remove` `.file-card-remove:hover` `.file-card-remove-over` `.file-card-remove-over:hover` `.file-card-row` `.file-card-thumb` `.file-card-tint` `.file-card-track`

```lua
local file_card = use "file-card"

ui.row { gap = "normal", wrap = true,
	file_card { name = "mockup.png", src = file.thumbnail, detail = "PNG · 840 KB",
		msg = { open = file.id }, remove = { remove = file.id } },
	file_card { name = "launch-plan.pdf", progress = upload.progress },
}
file_card { name = "notes.md", detail = "Markdown · 3 KB", layout = "row", remove = { remove = "notes" } }
```

#### `file-icon`

**File Icon.** A file's or folder's icon, coloured by its type, as an editor's file tree shows it.

#### `forecast-chart`

**Forecast Chart.** Bars over periods with each change above them, a dashed floor with the held part hatched, the low period flagged, and a value axis.

**When:** A balance or capacity projected over weeks or months against a minimum (cash against a floor, stock against a reorder point). For counts per bucket, stacked by kind, use `bar-chart`; for a small trend use `sparkline` or `ui.line`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `bar` | each bar's width in pixels (default 28) |
| `bars` | list of { label, value, delta? ("+9.2"), note? (text over the bar instead), current? (drawn dark), low? (flagged), tooltip? } |
| `event` | key of the message a bar sends: { [event] = index }; none without it |
| `floor` | a value drawn across, dashed; the part of each bar under it is hatched |
| `height` | the plot's height in pixels (default 260) |
| `max` | the value at the top of the plot |
| `ticks` | axis labels from the top (max) down to 0, evenly spaced |
| `to` | mod to send it to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.forecast` `.forecast-axis` `.forecast-bar` `.forecast-current` `.forecast-delta` `.forecast-fill` `.forecast-floor` `.forecast-held` `.forecast-label` `.forecast-label-low` `.forecast-label-now` `.forecast-low` `.forecast-low-text` `.forecast-tick` `.forecast-up`

```lua
local forecast_chart = use "forecast-chart"

forecast_chart { bars = { { current = true, delta = "$46.8M", label = "Today", low = false, value = 46.8 }, { current = false, delta = "−2.8", label = "Nov 2", low = false, value = 44 }, { current = false, delta = "+9.2", label = "Nov 9", low = false, value = 53.2 }, { current = false, delta = "−16.8", label = "Nov 16", low = false, value = 36.4 }, { current = false, delta = "−15.3", label = "Nov 23", low = true, value = 21.1 }, { current = false, delta = "+11.9", label = "Nov 30", low = false, value = 33 } }, floor = 15, height = 160, max = 60, ticks = { "$60M", "$30M", "$0" } }
```

#### `gantt`

**Gantt.** Tasks as bars over days: names on the left, months and days on top, progress inside each bar, dependency arrows, milestones, weekends shaded and a line on today; bars drag to move and stretch.

**When:** A project's schedule or timeline: when tasks run, how far they are, what waits on what. For events placed in hours use `week-calendar`; for a dated list of events use `timeline`; for a board by status use `kanban-column`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `day_width` | pixels per column (default 32) |
| `days` | the columns, oldest first: { label ("12"), month? (shown from this day on, "October 2026"), weekend?, today? }; a column can stand for a week too |
| `deps` | arrows from a task to one that waits on it: { from = id, to = id } |
| `event` | key of the message a task's name sends, default "select": { select = id } |
| `grow` | fill the parent and scroll the rows |
| `height` | pixels: the rows scroll within it |
| `label_width` | pixels for the names (default 220) |
| `move` | key of the message a bar's drag sends, default "move": { move = id, phase, value }, `value` the whole columns moved; on `up` with `value = 0` it was a click |
| `moving` | the drag in progress, drawn without changing the dates: { id, days, resize? }; apply it on `up` |
| `resize` | key of the message a drag of a bar's right edge sends, default "resize": the same, for the last day |
| `row_height` | pixels per row (default 36) |
| `rows` | a task { id, label, start, finish (column indexes from 1, the last included), progress? (0 to 1), color?, avatar? (a name), done?, milestone? (a diamond on `start`) }, or a heading { heading, count?, color? } |
| `selected` | id of the chosen task |
| `to` | mod to send them to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.gantt` `.gantt-bar` `.gantt-bar:selected` `.gantt-bar-after` `.gantt-bar-text` `.gantt-count` `.gantt-day` `.gantt-day-today` `.gantt-day-weekend` `.gantt-grip` `.gantt-group` `.gantt-head` `.gantt-heading` `.gantt-milestone` `.gantt-month` `.gantt-name` `.gantt-name:hover` `.gantt-name:selected` `.gantt-names` `.gantt-row` `.gantt-today` `.gantt-weekend`

```lua
local gantt = use "gantt"

gantt {
	days = state.days, -- { { label = "12", month = "October 2026", weekend = false, today = true }, ... }
	rows = {
		{ heading = "In Progress", count = 1 },
		{ id = "nav", label = "Finalize navigation", start = 2, finish = 9, progress = 0.6, color = "#8b5cf6", avatar = "Tanjim Islam" },
	},
	deps = { { from = "nav", to = "handoff" } },
	selected = state.selected, moving = state.moving, grow = true,
}
-- update: msg.select picks a task. msg.move and msg.resize carry the task's
-- id, `phase` and `value` (whole days): keep { id, days = value, resize }
-- as state.moving while it moves, add it to the dates on "up" and clear it.
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/gantt.luau`.

**Guide Card.** A guide, article or course in a grid: a pastel band with an icon, the category in colour, the title, the read time, and progress, Done or New.

For one featured course with actions use `course-card`; for a plain titled box use `card`; for a linked record inside a message use `record-card`.

#### `heat-grid`

**Heat Grid.** A contribution grid of rounded squares: columns filled from the bottom by a count, or shaded cell by cell by level, with labels under the ends.

**When:** Activity over days or weeks at a glance: lessons per week, posts per day, a streak, a course's progress as squares. For a GitHub-style calendar of days with months and weekdays use `contribution-graph`; for a count compared with the period before use `dot-chart`; for stacked counts with an axis use `bar-chart`; for one fraction use `meter` or `progress`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `color` | the filled colour (default accent) |
| `columns` | list, left to right; each a count (squares filled from the bottom) or a list of levels from the top (0 empty, 1 to `levels` lighter to full) |
| `empty` | an empty square's colour (default muted-foreground at 10%) |
| `gap` | pixels between squares (default 4) |
| `labels` | texts under the grid, spread from the first column to the last |
| `levels` | shades for level lists (default 4); counts use the full colour |
| `rows` | squares per column (default: the tallest column) |
| `size` | a square's side in pixels (default 13) |
| `spread` | columns spread across the parent's width, the first and last at its edges |
| `tooltips` | one text per column, shown under the pointer |

**Styles:** `.heat-grid` `.heat-grid-cell` `.heat-grid-label`

```lua
local heat_grid = use "heat-grid"

-- Counts, filled from the bottom:
heat_grid { rows = 3, columns = { 1, 0, 1, 0, 0, 2, 1, 0, 3, 1, 1, 1 },
	spread = true, size = 16, labels = { "Oct 5", "This week" } }
-- Levels, cell by cell (a single row of eight, two shades):
heat_grid { levels = 2, columns = { { 2 }, { 2 }, { 2 }, { 1 }, { 0 }, { 0 }, { 0 }, { 0 } } }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/heat-grid.luau`.

#### `histogram`

**Histogram.** Filled curves of counts across a range, one per channel and overlaid in their colours, with optional log scale and markers that can be dragged along it.

**When:** The spread of a picture's tones (red, green, blue, luminance), of latencies or of scores, where the shape matters more than any count; with draggable markers it is a levels control. For counts per labelled bucket use `bar-chart`; for a trend over time use `ui.line` or `series-chart`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `channels` | list of { values (counts, evenly spread from the range's start to its end), color?, name? }, drawn first to last |
| `drag` | message a marker's drag sends, with `marker` (its id), `value` (0 to 1) and `phase` added; markers are fixed without it |
| `height` | pixels (default 96) |
| `log` | scale counts by their logarithm, so small ones still show |
| `markers` | list of { id, value (0 to 1 along the range), color?, tooltip? }: lines across it |
| `max` | the count at the top (default the largest) |
| `shade` | dim what lies outside the first and last marker |
| `to` | mod to send `drag` to, if not the drawing one |
| `width` | pixels (default 256) |

**Styles:** `.histogram` `.histogram-grip` `.histogram-knob` `.histogram-marker` `.histogram-shade`

```lua
local histogram = use "histogram"

histogram { channels = { { color = "#ef4444", values = { 2, 6, 14, 30, 52, 70, 64, 48, 40, 52, 66, 50, 30, 16, 8, 3 } }, { color = "#22c55e", values = { 1, 4, 10, 22, 40, 60, 74, 66, 50, 44, 46, 38, 24, 12, 5, 2 } }, { color = "#3b82f6", values = { 4, 10, 22, 40, 58, 62, 50, 40, 36, 34, 30, 22, 14, 8, 4, 1 } } }, height = 90, markers = { { id = "shadow", value = 0.08 }, { id = "highlight", value = 0.9 } }, shade = true, width = 256 }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/histogram.luau`.

#### `kbd`

**Kbd.** Key caps for a shortcut, from a list of keys or a string like "cmd-shift-p" drawn with macOS glyphs.

**When:** Show a keyboard shortcut: in a menu row, a palette result, a tooltip line or a help sheet. Inside menus `menu` already draws one from an item's `shortcut`; for a word-like tag use `ui.badge`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `keys` | list of key labels ({ "⌘", "⇧", "P" }), or a string "cmd-shift-p"; spaces separate chords ("cmd-k cmd-s"). Names map to macOS glyphs: cmd/secondary ⌘, shift ⇧, alt/option ⌥, ctrl ⌃, enter ↩, tab ⇥, backspace ⌫, delete ⌦, arrows ↑↓←→, escape esc; single letters are upper-cased |
| `plain` | glyphs only, no cap borders (as in a macOS menu) |
| `small` | smaller caps, for menu rows |

**Styles:** `.kbd` `.kbd-chord` `.kbd-key` `.kbd-plain` `.kbd-small`

```lua
local kbd = use "kbd"

kbd { keys = "cmd-shift-p" }          -- ⌘ ⇧ P
kbd { keys = { "⌘", "K" } }
kbd { keys = "cmd-k cmd-s", small = true }
kbd { keys = "ctrl-tab", plain = true }
```

**KPI Meter.** A headline figure with a dot and title, the value beside a caption, a bar of rounded segments and a mono legend.

#### `line-chart`

**Line Chart.** Solid and dashed lines over periods with faint columns behind, an axis, labels, and a picked period with a rule, dots and a floating card.

**When:** A measure over days or weeks compared with a forecast or a target (actual against predicted, this year against last), where the user picks a day to read its figures. For several readings on one scale with a legend and a crosshair use `series-chart`; for bars against a floor use `forecast-chart`; for stacked counts use `bar-chart`; for a bare trend use `ui.line` or `sparkline`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `bars` | faint columns behind the lines, one value per period |
| `card` | element floating beside the picked period (its figures) |
| `card_width` | the card's width in pixels, to keep it inside the plot (default 170) |
| `event` | key of the message a period sends, default "point": { point = index } |
| `height` | the plot's height in pixels (default 180) |
| `labels` | one label per period, under the plot |
| `max` | the value at the top of the plot |
| `min` | the value at the bottom (default 0) |
| `selected` | index of the picked period: a rule, dots, and `card` |
| `series` | list of { name?, points (one per period), color? (default accent), dashed? }; the first is drawn under the next |
| `ticks` | axis labels from the top (max) down to the bottom, evenly spaced |
| `tips` | tooltip text per period, shown under the pointer |
| `to` | mod to send it to, if not the drawing one |
| `width` | the plot's width in pixels (default 600) |

**Styles:** `.line-chart` `.line-chart-bar` `.line-chart-base` `.line-chart-card` `.line-chart-label` `.line-chart-label-on` `.line-chart-marker` `.line-chart-point` `.line-chart-rule` `.line-chart-slot` `.line-chart-slot:hover` `.line-chart-tick`

#### `message-header`

**Message Header.** An open message's header: the subject large, the sender's avatar, name and a copyable address chip, To and Cc lines, and the date with actions.

**When:** Above the body of an email or a thread's message in a reading pane. For a row in the message list use `mail-row`; for a comment in a review use `comment-card`; for a chat turn use `chat-message`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `[children]` | anything under the header, before its line: a follow-up `banner`, a Translate button |
| `actions` | elements after the date (icon buttons: show images, more) |
| `avatar` | an image file for the avatar instead of the initials |
| `cc` | copied to: a name or a list of names |
| `color` | the avatar's colour instead of the one picked from the name |
| `date` | when it was sent, as shown ("Oct 16, 2026 at 4:12 PM") |
| `email` | the sender's address, in a chip that copies it on a click |
| `from` | the sender's name; the avatar's initials and colour come from it |
| `recipients` | who it went to: a name, or a list of names ("To: Sam Lee") |
| `sender` | message a click on the sender's name sends (open the contact) |
| `subject` | the subject, as the pane's title; none for a later message in a thread |
| `to` | mod to send `sender` to, if not the drawing one |

**Styles:** `.message-header` `.message-header-date` `.message-header-email` `.message-header-email:hover` `.message-header-from` `.message-header-name` `.message-header-name:hover` `.message-header-subject` `.message-header-to`

```lua
local message_header = use "message-header"
local icon_button = use "icon-button"

message_header {
	subject = m.subject, from = m.from, email = m.email,
	recipients = m.to, cc = m.cc, date = m.date,
	actions = { icon_button { icon = "image", tooltip = "Show images", msg = "images", size = "small" } },
	ui.row { justify = "end", ui.button { "Translate", icon = "sparkles", small = true, variant = "outline", msg = "translate" } },
}
```

#### `meter`

**Meter.** A bar filled to a fraction from 0 to 1, with the percentage beside it; it warns past a threshold.

**When:** A fraction (0 to 1) as a bar with its percentage: memory, quota, progress of a known size. For work with no known size use `progress` with `busy`; for a narrow upright bar in a tight row use `vertical-bar`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | text before the bar |
| `percent` | false hides the percentage |
| `value` | 0 to 1 |
| `warn` | fraction past which it shows the warning color |
| `width` | bar width in pixels |

**Styles:** `.meter-fill` `.meter-hot` `.meter-label` `.meter-percent` `.meter-track`

```lua
local meter = use "meter"

meter { label = "Memory", value = 0.62, width = 48 }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/meter.luau`.

#### `metric`

**Metric.** A label, a value set large (or very large), and a note under it in a tone.

**When:** Headline figures across the top of a dashboard card: cash today, the lowest week, a total. For a figure in its own tile with a trend use `stat-tile`; for a status bar reading use `stat`; for a fraction use `meter`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `label` | what it is |
| `note` | a line under it |
| `size` | "normal" (default) or "hero": the card's main figure |
| `tone` | the note's tone: success, danger, warning or muted (default) |
| `value` | the figure, as text |

**Styles:** `.metric` `.metric-hero` `.metric-label` `.metric-note` `.metric-value`

```lua
local metric = use "metric"

metric { label = "Lowest week", note = "Week of Jan 4", value = "$26.4M" }
```

#### `mini-bars`

**Mini Bars.** A few small labelled bars, one highlighted, future ones hatched: a figure by period at a glance.

**When:** A figure over a few periods in a KPI strip or a card header (revenue by month, signups by week). For a live trend in a status bar use `sparkline`; for a full chart with an axis use `bar-chart` or `forecast-chart`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `bar` | each bar's width in pixels (default 18) |
| `bars` | list of { label, value, future? } |
| `height` | the tallest bar's height in pixels (default 40) |
| `highlight` | index of the bar to stand out (default the last that is not future) |

**Styles:** `.mini-bars` `.mini-bars-bar` `.mini-bars-future` `.mini-bars-label` `.mini-bars-on`

```lua
local mini_bars = use "mini-bars"

mini_bars { bars = { { future = false, label = "Jul", value = 18 }, { future = false, label = "Aug", value = 26 }, { future = false, label = "Sep", value = 21 }, { future = false, label = "Oct", value = 33 }, { future = false, label = "Nov", value = 41 }, { future = true, label = "Dec", value = 38 } } }
```

#### `note-card`

**Note Card.** A numbered review note: yellow numbered circle, file:line, text and a × remove button; selectable.

**When:** Notes a person leaves on lines while reviewing, to send to an agent; list them in a column beside a `diff-view`. For an authored comment use `comment-card`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `event` | click message key instead of "select": sends { [event] = id } |
| `id` | the note's id, sent in messages (default its number) |
| `location` | file:line it points at |
| `number` | shown in the circle |
| `remove` | × message key instead of "remove": sends { [remove] = id } |
| `selected` | highlight it |
| `text` | the note |
| `to` | the mod to send them to |

**Styles:** `.note-card` `.note-card:hover` `.note-card:selected` `.note-card-location` `.note-card-number` `.note-card-number-text` `.note-card-remove` `.note-card-remove:hover` `.note-card-remove-icon` `.note-card-text`

```lua
local note_card = use "note-card"

note_card { location = "src/ledger.rs:26", number = 1, text = "Reject mixing currencies here: return a Result instead of silently grouping." }
```

A whole mod using it, with state: `app/components/demos/note-card.luau`.

#### `numbered-list`

**Numbered List.** Items in order, numbered in a muted column, wrapping text aligned.

**When:** Ordered steps or suggestions in a message, a note or a help page. For a checklist use `task-row`; for events in time use `timeline`.

| Prop | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `items` | the items' text |
| `start` | the first number (default 1) |

**Styles:** `.numbered-list` `.numbered-list-item` `.numbered-list-number`

```lua
local numbered_list = use "numbered-list"

numbered_list { items = { "Send the revised pricing deck", "Book a call with procurement", "Offer a two-year term" } }
```
